data.title: Building the System/360 Mainframe Nearly Destroyed IBM
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: IBM's System/360 (S/360), introduced in 1964, was a transformative mainframe series that revolutionized computing and business operations, despite nearly destroying IBM during its development. The project cost US$5 billion and involved creating a line of 150 products, including 9-track magnetic tape drives. Before the S/360, IBM's popular 1401 mainframe could not be expanded or upgraded, leading to customer demand for compatible and upgradable systems. Internal rivalry between IBM's Endicott and Poughkeepsie engineering teams further complicated matters, as their systems were incompatible. To stay competitive and reduce R&D costs, IBM decided to develop the S/360, aiming for a unified system that could handle various tasks and grow with customer needs. The development process was chaotic, marked by internal conflicts and technological uncertainties, but ultimately succeeded, changing the course of computing history. The S/360's success cemented IBM's leadership and enabled the widespread adoption of computers in the Information Age.

43619229.article_content:
History of Technology
Feature
Building the System/360 Mainframe Nearly Destroyed IBM
Instead, the S/360 proved to be the most successful product launch ever and changed the course of computing
James W. Cortada
05 Apr 2019
15 min read
IBM spent US $5 billion to build the System/360, introduced in 1964. These 9-track magnetic tape drives were among the S/360’s 150-product line.
Photo: Mark Richards/Computer History Museum
A short list of the most transformative products
of the past century and a half would include the lightbulb, Ford’s Model T—and the
IBM System/360
. This
mainframe
series forever changed the computer industry and revolutionized how businesses and governments worked, enhancing productivity and making countless new tasks possible.
In the years leading up to its 7 April 1964 launch, however, the 360 was one of the scariest dramas in American business. It took a nearly fanatical commitment at all levels of
IBM
to bring forth this remarkable collection of machines and software. While the technological innovations that went into the S/360 were important, how they were created and deployed bordered on disaster. The company experienced what
science policy expert Keith Pavitt called “tribal warfare”
: people clashing and collaborating in a rapidly growing company with unstable, and in some instances unknown, technologies, as uncertainty and ambiguity dogged all the protagonists.
Ultimately,
IBM
was big and diverse enough in talent, staffing, financing, and materiel to succeed. In an almost entrepreneurial fashion, it took advantage of emerging technologies, no matter where they were located within the enterprise. In hindsight, it seemed a sloppy and ill-advised endeavor, chaotic in execution and yet brilliantly successful. We live in an age that celebrates innovation, so examining cases of how innovation is done can only illuminate our understanding of the process.
By the end of the 1950s,
computer users faced a seemingly intractable problem. Had it not been solved, it would have prevented computers from becoming widespread, and any thoughts of living in an Information Age would have been fiction.
The S/360 was designed to replace IBM’s 1401 mainframe, which was popular but couldn’t be expanded or upgraded.
Photo: IBM
Organizations were acquiring computers in great numbers, automating many of the old punch card operations and doing more with data processing. The popularity of the IBM 1401 illustrates the rapid adoption of computing. Over 12,000 of these systems were sold from their introduction in 1959 to 1971, when IBM retired the line.
With the 1401 so dominating the computer business, any problems with it were serious. One of them was that the 1401 was too small.
Users found these machines so useful that they kept piling more work on them, reaching the system’s capacity. They then had three options: move to a bigger IBM system, such as an IBM 7000, install a competitor’s system, or acquire more 1401s. None of these options was attractive. To change to a bigger system required rewriting software, since the old software would not work on a different type of machine. The cost of rewriting could easily exceed the financial benefits of moving to a bigger machine. Such a change also called for retraining staff or hiring new staff familiar with the new system. Adding more units of the same system was equally unattractive because each unit required duplicate staff, equipment, and maintenance of hardware and software. Customers wanted systems that were “upgradable” or “compatible,” such that as their needs grew, they could bring in larger machines but still run the same software and peripheral equipment. In the 1950s and early 1960s, it was a wish, and for vendors an aspiration.
IBM had worse problems than its customers did. The 1401s were proving so popular that engineers in Endicott, N.Y., which had developed the system, resisted attempts by their counterparts in Poughkeepsie to build larger computers, leading to growing rivalry between the two groups. As one engineer recalled, “So intense was it that sometimes it seemed to exceed the rivalry with external competitors.” Systems made by Poughkeepsie would not run programs written for the 1400 series. Customers wanting to move from the smaller 1400s to the larger Poughkeepsie machines put increasing pressure on IBM to provide compatibility. Senior management had to contend with the expenses of sustaining R&D for a half-dozen incompatible product lines and training IBMers to sell and maintain so many systems.
Consensus grew that IBM needed to get down to one system to simplify production, reduce the cost of R&D, and be more competitive against a growing array of rivals. If customers had to upgrade in the early 1960s, they could just as easily move to a competitor’s machine, since they would have to rewrite their software anyway.
The power of compatibility was demonstrated in the fall of 1960, when IBM introduced the more powerful 1410 to replace the 1401. S

data.title: Solving a “Layton Puzzle” with Prolog
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者在重写《逻辑编程语言》章节时，计划用更实用的例子替代经典的逻辑谜题演示，如八皇后问题和四色问题。作者提到，虽然展示谜题解法在时事通讯中很酷，但他希望例子更具实用性。接着，他讨论了使用Prolog解决一个电子游戏谜题，该谜题涉及根据给定学生的得分推断出第四个学生的答案。

作者详细解释了Prolog代码，展示了如何定义评分规则，并利用递归计算学生的得分。Prolog的逻辑谓词具有双向性，不仅可以验证得分，还能推导可能的答案。最后，作者改进了程序，确保答案键的长度和元素类型符合要求。整个过程展示了Prolog在解决逻辑问题上的强大功能和灵活性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同方法解决逻辑谜题的可行性及优缺点，特别是使用Prolog及其他工具如Z3、约束满足问题（CSP）等。

不同观点：
• **tannhaeuser**：认为文章使用SWI Prolog的约束库解决谜题是多余的，因为问题可以通过纯ISO Prolog轻松解决，并提供了Pablo的解决方案链接。强调了直接执行Prolog代码的简便性。
• **taeric**：对谜题表示兴趣，并提到Knuth关于约束满足的讨论。建议将实际问题与儿童谜题类比，以增加趣味性，鼓励更多类似讨论。
• **a_e_k**：展示了使用Z3Py（一个SAT求解器）的解决方案，以简洁的代码实现了问题求解，并承认自己并非Z3专家，可能有更优解法。
• **NooneAtAll3**：提供了一种“人工”解法，通过逻辑推理和代数方程逐步推导出谜题答案，展示了不依赖编程工具的解题思路。
• **Avshalom**：分享了另一种Prolog解决方案，指出在不同Prolog环境（如Ciao Prolog）中需要加载额外模块。也提供了代码示例。
• **crtasm**：简单提到谜题来源于《雷顿教授》游戏系列，未深入讨论解法。
• **AceJohnny2**：引用了Hacker News上关于Prolog为何失去流行的讨论，并通过个人经历说明了Prolog在解决某些逻辑谜题上的有效性。
• **jodrellblank**：提供了可以在SWISH（SWI Prolog在线环境）中运行的Prolog代码，展示了如何利用约束求解器解决谜题，并给出了具体操作步骤。
• **trainyperson**：建议通过“纸笔”逻辑推理解决谜题，认为无需依赖约束求解工具，强调了逻辑推理过程的趣味性和可操作性。
• **jfengel**：认为谜题可以通过暴力求解，但对新手来说可能过于复杂。询问是否存在纯演绎的解法，以减少试错空间。
• **superlopuh**：分享了使用Sentient语言解决类似谜题的经历，认为其比Prolog更符合人体工程学，但Sentient项目已多年未更新，表示遗憾。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是使用Prolog的约束库是否必要，tannhaeuser认为纯Prolog即可解决问题，而其他人如jodrellblank和Avshalom则展示了使用约束库的解决方案。
• 不同工具和方法的优缺点被讨论，如Z3Py和Prolog的对比，以及人工推理与自动化工具的取舍。
• 对新手友好性的考虑也被提及，trainyperson和jfengel都关注了谜题对新手的难度问题，并提出了不同的简化解决方案。
• 一些评论提到了相关资源和外部讨论，如Knuth的书和Hacker News上的讨论，扩展了话题的范围。

April 8, 2025
Solving a "Layton Puzzle" with Prolog
I have a lot in the works for the this month's
Logic for Programmers
release. Among other things, I'm completely rewriting the chapter on Logic Programming Languages.
I originally showcased the paradigm with puzzle solvers, like
eight queens
or
four-coloring
. Lots of other demos do this too! It takes creativity and insight for humans to solve them, so a program doing it feels magical. But I'm trying to write a book about practical techniques and I want everything I talk about to be
useful
. So in v0.9 I'll be replacing these examples with a couple of new programs that might get people thinking that Prolog could help them in their day-to-day work.
On the other hand, for a newsletter, showcasing a puzzle solver is pretty cool. And recently I stumbled into
this post
by my friend
Pablo Meier
, where he solves a videogame puzzle with Prolog:
1
Summary for the text-only readers: We have a test with 10 true/false questions (denoted
a/b
) and four student attempts. Given the scores of the first three students, we have to figure out the fourth student's score.

baaababaaa = 5
baaabbbaba = 3
bbaaabbaaa = ???
You can see Pablo's solution
here
, and try it in SWI-prolog
here
. Pretty cool! But after way too long studying Prolog just to write this dang book chapter, I wanted to see if I could do it more elegantly than him. Code and puzzle spoilers to follow.

• **crtasm**：简单提到谜题来源于《雷顿教授》游戏系列，未深入讨论解法。
• **AceJohnny2**：引用了Hacker News上关于Prolog为何失去流行的讨论，并通过个人经历说明了Prolog在解决某些逻辑谜题上的有效性。
• **jodrellblank**：提供了可以在SWISH（SWI Prolog在线环境）中运行的Prolog代码，展示了如何利用约束求解器解决谜题，并给出了具体操作步骤。
• **trainyperson**：建议通过“纸笔”逻辑推理解决谜题，认为无需依赖约束求解工具，强调了逻辑推理过程的趣味性和可操作性。
• **jfengel**：认为谜题可以通过暴力求解，但对新手来说可能过于复杂。询问是否存在纯演绎的解法，以减少试错空间。
• **superlopuh**：分享了使用Sentient语言解决类似谜题的经历，认为其比Prolog更符合人体工程学，但Sentient项目已多年未更新，表示遗憾。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是使用Prolog的约束库是否必要，tannhaeuser认为纯Prolog即可解决问题，而其他人如jodrellblank和Avshalom则展示了使用约束库的解决方案。
• 不同工具和方法的优缺点被讨论，如Z3Py和Prolog的对比，以及人工推理与自动化工具的取舍。
• 对新手友好性的考虑也被提及，trainyperson和jfengel都关注了谜题对新手的难度问题，并提出了不同的简化解决方案。
• 一些评论提到了相关资源和外部讨论，如Knuth的书和Hacker News上的讨论，扩展了话题的范围。

data.title: PostgreSQL Full-Text Search: Fast When Done Right (Debunking the Slow Myth)
data.author: VoVAllen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres 全文搜索（FTS）的性能、优化及其与其他搜索系统（如Elasticsearch）的对比

不同观点：
• **[retakeming]**：作为pg_search的维护者，认为Postgres文档中同时认可多种优化策略。pg_search的目的是解决如何让Postgres在各种复杂查询（如布尔、模糊、分面、相关性排序等）上达到Elasticsearch级别的性能，而不是针对单一查询的优化。Neon/ParadeDB的基准测试包含12个查询，虽然可以通过创建复合索引等方法优化，但这些方法在实际应用中不现实。pg_search提供了一种简单的索引定义，无需用户对每个文本列进行重复操作。

• **[danpalmer]**：批评了Neon/ParadeDB文章中的基准测试方法，认为其错误在于动态计算tsvector，而Postgres文档中已经明确说明了如何优化查询性能。他认为这种错误要么是故意误导，要么是由于没有仔细阅读文档。

• **[nattaylor]**：关注查询计划（explain plans），提到如果查询使用了索引，那么动态重新检查tsvector只会在匹配项上进行，且由于查询限制了返回10条数据，因此重新检查的数量有限。但如果查询在两个GIN索引上有条件，则可能导致不必要的工作。

• **[nostrebored]**：质疑为什么人们希望把所有功能（如向量搜索、全文搜索、工作负载编排、队列等）都放入Postgres中，不理解这种趋势。

• **[zhousun]**：支持更多“Postgres原生”的全文搜索实现，认为像Lucene/Tantivy这样的解决方案由于设计初衷不同，与Postgres的堆表结合时效果不佳。

• **[some_developer]**：分享了多年前尝试使用Postgres原生FTS失败的经历，由于在插入频繁的表上添加索引导致事务超时，最终不得不放弃。

• **[atemerev]**：认为1000万条记录是一个玩具数据集，建议使用更大的数据集（如完整的维基百科或Reddit评论）来进行基准测试以获得更有意义的比较。

• **[ltbarcly3]**：认为Postgres全文搜索过于僵化，无法进行复杂调优，如子字符串搜索、自定义分词等，而Solr和Elasticsearch在这方面提供了更强的配置能力。Postgres的FTS系统被视为一个简单的玩具系统，无法满足复杂需求。

补充讨论：
• **[chenhoey1211]**：提到很多团队直接选择Elasticsearch或Meilisearch，而忽视了Postgres原生FTS的潜力，并提出SQLite+FTS5+Wasm是否能在浏览器中提供类似的性能表现，作为离线优先应用的方向。

• **[briankelly]**：认为问题不在于速度，而在于规模，建议在系统达到极限之前继续使用。

• **[Thaxll]**：认为定制的Postgres代码不能称之为“原生”。

• **[Sytten]**：认为这种内容营销对于像ParadeDB这样的初创公司来说是一个很好的宣传方式。

争议焦点：
• Postgres FTS的优化方法及其实用性。
• 是否应该将所有功能集成到Postgres中。
• Postgres FTS与其他搜索系统（如Elasticsearch）在灵活性和性能上的比较。

data.title: The Barium Experiment
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GUI工具包的设计、选择以及对现有工具（如GTK、Qt）的评价

不同观点：
• [nine_k] 认为，专注于Xlib且使用Common Lisp编写的GUI工具包（如Barium）因为不考虑兼容性问题，可以更精简高效。同时，对GTK模仿苹果将 scrollbars 隐藏的设计选择表示不满。
• [zombot] 反对被局限于某种特定的生态系统（暗指Gnome/GTK），并认为这种限制代价高昂。
• [rtpg] 认为Qt/KDE在避免Gnome/GTK相关问题上表现更好，但承认Qt本身也比较"笨重"。
• [userbinator] 提到GUI框架的快速变化（churn）迫使开发者不断修改旧代码，并认为Win32 (+WINE) 是一个更稳定的GUI API选择。
• [nsm] 推荐Racket语言的GUI实现，认为其成熟且跨平台，尤其是与GTK集成良好，适用于教学IDE等场景。
• [boxed] 认为NeXTStep仍然领先于大多数现代GUI框架。
• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 对重新发明GUI框架表示兴趣，但认为使用非LISP语言绑定到Barium的实际应用可能性不大。
• [jeffbee] 不理解为什么从GTK2迁移到GTK3会被视为灾难，并质疑为何开发者必须被迫跟随这种"变化"。
• [DeathArrow] 认为使用现有GUI框架（如GTK、Qt等）进行开发困难且容易出错，不具备未来可持续性，因此有人选择自己开发工具包，但这往往是出于实验或乐趣。
• [snvzz] 对Barium这样的新工具包表示支持，希望其能够持久发展，而非像其他流行工具包那样迅速膨胀和消亡。
• [duskwuff] 解释GTK等工具包随时间演变的原因，指出Linux桌面环境的变化导致UI库也需要适应新的硬件和需求，认为期望UI库20多年不变是不现实的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于开发者是否应被"强迫"跟随GUI框架的演变（如GTK2到GTK3的迁移），以及现有框架如GTK和Qt的优缺点。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同开发者对稳定性和新颖性的不同追求，一些开发者倾向于选择老旧但稳定的API（如Win32），而另一些开发者则寻求创新和实验性技术（如Barium、Racket）。
• 对图形和单位标注的正确性也有一个小讨论，[yohbho] 指出学术论文中常见的标注错误，反映出对细节的关注。

data.title: DIY experimental reactor harnesses the Birkeland-Eyde process
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由公民科学家Marb自制的实验反应器，利用Birkeland-Eyde过程通过电弧将空气中的氮转化为硝酸。该过程曾在化肥生产中使用，但由于高能耗在一百年前被淘汰。Marb主要出于对科学的兴趣，使用Arduino UNO Rev3控制反应器，通过 breakout shield 调节电弧电源，并使用传感器监控反应条件。尽管该过程效率不高，Marb的设计重点在于空气干燥和电弧控制。他展示了一次实验演示，并表示如果有足够兴趣，会制作更详细的 follow-up 视频。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过特定技术或设备生成硝酸及其应用的可能性和潜在问题

不同观点：
• **ashoeafoot** 认为是否有必要使用长弧来生成表面，并建议是否可以采用分形表面来实现弧形和隔离效果，可能在质疑当前方法的复杂性或效率。

• **mikewarot** 指出，当能源的边际成本接近零时，效率问题变得不那么重要。这一观点表明，如果使用多余的太阳能，该技术在离网情况下尤其有价值，暗示该方法在特定条件下是可行的。

• **8474_s** 强调该技术的潜在应用，认为它可以实现闭环系统，补充通常需要氮固定的土壤，这表明该技术在农业和生态系统维护方面可能有重要作用。

• **dfedbeef** 提出担忧，认为在YouTube上发布此类操作的详细步骤可能不是个好主意，因为硝酸是某些受到严格监管和危险的物质的前体，暗示可能存在安全隐患或法律问题。

• **NoMoreNicksLeft** 提到YouTube上的Andreas the Alchemist有一个升级版的设备，每天能生产大约一加仑的硝酸，且浓度接近发烟硝酸，但耗电量高达5千瓦时，提供了实际案例来对比效率和产出。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于生成硝酸的步骤公开是否合适，以及该技术在实际应用中的效率和安全性。
• 实际应用中的例子（如Andreas the Alchemist的设备）提供了有关当前技术水平和能耗的重要信息。
• 讨论还涉及到该技术的潜在应用场景，如离网能源利用和农业生态系统维护。

This DIY experimental reactor harnesses the Birkeland-Eyde process
Arduino Team
—
March 17th, 2025
Nitrogen is critical for farming at scale and without some form of nitrogen to enrich the soil, we couldn’t grow staple crops efficiently enough to feed our large global population. Serious science goes into the production of fertilizers and the Birkeland-Eyde process was one early example. It uses electrical arcs to turn nitrogen in the air into nitric acid. Marb is an enthusiastic citizen scientist and built his own experimental reactor to harness the Birkeland-Eyde process.
The Birkeland-Eyde process was largely phased out a century ago, because it is inefficient due to the high energy requirements. It needs a lot of energy to create the electric arcs — too much energy to be practical at the scale necessary for modern industrial farming. But efficiency isn’t a major concern for Marb, who is more interested in the science than fertilizer production.
Creating an electrical arc isn’t very difficult, but controlling it is more challenging. For that reason, Marb used an
Arduino UNO Rev3
to oversee his DIY reactor. Through a breakout shield, the Arduino controls the flow of power to the arc electrodes. That requires a large power supply, transformers, and a boost converter.
The rest of the reactor is devoted to the containment, preparation, and flow of air. The Birkeland-Eyde process works best with dry air, so Marb’s design pumps air through a desiccant-packed tube and into the reaction chamber where the electrodes meet. Sensors, like a temperature sensor, help the Arduino gain feedback on the conditions.
Marb’s video ends with a demonstration, but he hasn’t yet refined the reaction process for maximum yields. If there is enough interest, Marb says that he’ll make a follow-up video with more detail.

43595193.article_content:
Breadcrumb
MIT News
A new way to make graphs more accessible to blind and low-vision readers
A new way to make graphs more accessible to blind and low-vision readers
The Tactile Vega-Lite system, developed at MIT CSAIL, streamlines the tactile chart design process; could help educators efficiently create these graphics and aid designers in making precise changes.
Alex Shipps
|
MIT CSAIL
Publication Date
:
March 25, 2025
Press Inquiries
Press Contact
:
Adam
Conner-Simons
Email:
aconner@csail.mit.edu
Phone:
617-324-9135
MIT Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence Lab
Close
Caption
:
The Tactile Vega-Lite system can take data from something like an Excel spreadsheet and turn it into both a standard visual chart and a touch-based one. Design standards are hardwired as default rules within the program, helping educators and designers automatically create accessible tactile charts.
Credits
:
Image: Alex Shipps/MIT CSAIL, with elements from Pixabay.
Previous image
Next image
Bar graphs and other charts provide a simple way to communicate data, but are, by definition, difficult to translate for readers who are blind or low-vision. Designers have developed methods for converting these visuals into “tactile charts,” but guidelines for doing so are extensive (for example, the Braille Authority of North America’s 2022 guidebook is 426 pages long). The process also requires understanding different types of software, as designers often draft their chart in programs like Adobe Illustrator and then translate it into Braille using another application.
Researchers from MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) have now developed an approach that streamlines the design process for tactile chart designers. Their program, called “Tactile Vega-Lite,” can take data from something like an Excel spreadsheet and turn it into both a standard visual chart and a touch-based one. Design standards are hardwired as default rules within the program to help educators and designers automatically create accessible tactile charts.
The tool could make it easier for blind and low-vision readers to understand many graphics, such as a bar chart comparing minimum wages across states or a line graph tracking countries’ GDPs over time. To bring your designs to the real world, you can tweak your chart in Tactile Vega-Lite and then send its file to a Braille embosser (which prints text as readable dots).
This spring, the researchers will present Tactile Vega-Lite in a
paper
at the Association of Computing Machinery Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems. According to lead author Mengzhu “Katie” Chen SM ’25, the tool strikes a balance between the precision that design professionals want for editing and the efficiency educators need to create tactile charts quickly.
“We interviewed teachers who wanted to make their lessons accessible to blind and low-vision students, and designers experienced in putting together tactile charts,” says Chen, a recent CSAIL affiliate and master's graduate in electrical engineering and computer science and the Program in System Design and Management. “Since their needs differ, we designed a program that’s easy to use, provides instant feedback when you want to make tweaks, and implements accessibility guidelines.”
Data you can feel
The researchers’ program builds off of their 2017 visualization tool
Vega-Lite
by automatically encoding both a flat, standard chart and a tactile one. Senior author and MIT postdoc Jonathan Zong SM ’20, PhD ’24 points out that the program makes intuitive design decisions so users don’t have to.
“Tactile Vega-Lite has smart defaults to ensure proper spacing, layout, and texture and Braille conversion, following best practices to create good touch-based reading experiences,” says Zong, who is also a fellow at the Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society at Harvard University and an incoming assistant professor at the University of Colorado. “Building on existing guidelines and our interviews with experts, the goal is for teachers or visual designers without a lot of tactile design expertise to quickly convey data in a clear way for tactile readers to explore and understand.”
Tactile Vega-Lite’s code editor allows users to customize axis labels, tick marks, and other elements. Different features within the chart are represented by abstractions — or summaries of a longer body of code — that can be modified. These shortcuts allow you to write brief phrases that tweak the design of your chart. For example, if you want to change how the bars in your graph are filled out, you could change the code in the “Texture” section from “dottedFill” to “verticalFill” to replace small circles with upward lines.
To understand how these abstractions work, the researchers added a gallery of examples. Each one includes a phrase and what change that code leads to. Still, the team is looking to refine Tactile Vega-Lite’s user interface to make it more accessible to users less

data.title: Hardening the Firefox Front End with Content Security Policies
data.author: evilpie
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了Firefox用户界面（UI）使用网页技术（如HTML、CSS和JavaScript）的优点和潜在安全风险，尤其是注入攻击（如XSS）。由于Firefox UI运行在父进程中，而网页内容在低权限的子进程中，正常情况下网页内容无法注入到父进程。然而，在Pwn2Own 2022比赛中，有参赛者利用漏洞逃逸出网页内容沙箱，通过在Firefox UI中创建JavaScript inline事件处理器实现攻击。

为防止此类攻击，Firefox团队借鉴网页安全措施，如内容安全策略（CSP），已从`browser.xhtml`中移除了超过600个inline事件处理器，并用`addEventListener`替代。此外，针对其他窗口和侧边栏，添加了更严格的CSP以增强安全性。这些措施显著提升了Firefox前端代码的安全性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CSP（内容安全策略）的有效性、实现问题以及在浏览器和扩展中的应用

不同观点：
• theandrewbailey：认为CSP在防止安全漏洞方面非常有效，但很多开发者和设计师没有认真对待，不正确地实现CSP（如不使用外部文件设置样式和脚本）。他主张应像反对表格布局一样反对内联样式和脚本。

• davidmurdoch：指出Firefox在扩展中的CSP存在长达9年的未修复bug，并提供了bug链接。他提到Mozilla的扩展商店不允许变通方案，尽管这已被确认为bug。

• lol768：表达了对浏览器DevTools和界面引入与网页相同安全问题的担忧，认为这是从XUL迁移后产生的新问题，类似于Electron中XSS变成RCE的问题。

• CamouflagedKiwi：对HTML设置带来的复杂生态系统表示担忧，认为浏览器需要对网页代码进行沙盒处理。尽管承认文章中提到的改进是好事情，但仍对潜在的权衡表示紧张。

• yanis_t：赞扬CSP在缓解安全问题和强制良好实践方面的作用，并分享了自己开发的CSP生成和验证工具链接。

• myfonj：惊讶于没有允许在初始载荷中设置内联事件处理器但禁用之后通过`setAttribute`设置的策略，认为这样可以保持静态表单功能并禁用恶意运行时模板。

• bbarnett：建议使用Firefox的配置文件功能来应对某些网站不兼容CSP的问题，并分享了自己在Linux上使用图标方便启动不同配置文件的经验。

• SebFender：认为CSP虽然有助于缓解一些安全问题，但通常可以通过简单的攻击绕过，尤其是在DOM管理和安全不佳的情况下。

• foobar9898989：以幽默的方式表达了对CSP在前端实现的看法，认为这是增加额外安全层的好事，但也提到浏览器安全进化的复杂性和挑战。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是CSP在实际应用中的有效性和浏览器厂商（如Mozilla）对其支持的及时性。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对内联样式和脚本的不同看法，以及如何在不影响功能的情况下限制它们的使用。
• 还有对浏览器DevTools和界面安全问题的深层次担忧，尤其是在从XUL迁移后引入的新问题。

通过这些观点，可以看出CSP在实际应用中的复杂性和多面性，以及不同开发者和用户对其的不同期望和需求。

43630388.article_content:
Most of the Firefox User Interface (UI), including the address bar and the tab strip, are implemented using standard web technologies like HTML, CSS and JavaScript plus some additional custom components like
XUL
. One of the advantages of using web technologies for the front end is that it allows rendering the frontend using the browser engine on all desktop operating systems. However, just like many web applications are susceptible to some form of injection attack (
OWASP Top Ten
), Firefox’s use of web technologies for the frontend makes it no exception and hence it is vulnerable to injection attacks as well.
The most well known type of injection attack are Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Like the name suggests, these attacks violate the boundary between different sites and circumvent first line security defenses like the
same-origin policy
. As with the existence of boundaries between different sites, the Firefox UI, which runs in the parent process, is separated from web content running in
lower-privileged content processes
. The sandboxed web content should not be able to inject content, especially code, into the parent process. Of course there needs to be some way for both parent and child processes to communicate with each other - otherwise it would, for example, be impossible to update a tab’s title in the UI after a web page sets its own document title. The way Firefox accomplishes this interaction is through a system called IPC -
inter-process communication
.
In Pwn2Own (a computer hacking contest) 2022 a participant managed to find a chain of exploits that allowed them to escape the web content sandbox (cf.
write-up by a ZDI employee
, a
generalized introduction
or
video by LifeOverflow
). A part of this exploit chain involved creating a JavaScript inline event handler (using setAttribute) in the Firefox UI, and then triggering the execution of that event handler. For websites, the well known approach of mitigating XSS attacks using inline event handlers usually involves using a
Content-Security-Policy
(CSP). CSP allows for restricting what scripts are allowed to execute on a given page. Typically by only allowing scripts from specific URLs, or with specific hashes. In particular, unless
‘unsafe-inline’
is specified, all attempts to define inline event handlers are blocked by the browser. And because the Firefox UI uses HTML with some special sauce, we can actually also use CSPs in the same way to harden the Firefox frontend code.
Progress
The main Firefox UI, which contains the tabs, address bar, menu bar etc. is actually just one big XHTML document called
browser.xhtml
. Recently we have removed in total over 600 inline event handlers across
50 bugs
from this XHTML document. At this point we want to acknowledge the support of the Firefox frontend team, without their co-operation we wouldn’t have been able to land so many changes in such a short amount of time.
Figure 1: Graph showing the number of inline event handlers in browser.xhtml over time in Firefox Nightly. The numbers were estimated using grep.
Interlude: How to replace inline event handlers
In case you are a Firefox developer, the maintainer of a Firefox fork like the Tor Browser, or just a web developer interested in securing your own website, the following might be relevant to you. The process of removing inline event handlers usually involves finding all the places that define an inline event handler like
<button onclick="buttonClicked()">
and then replacing this with a call to
addEventListener
from a new JS file. Roughly like this:
let
button
=
document
.
querySelector
(
"
button
"
);
button
.
addEventListener
(
"
click
"
,
buttonClicked
);
However there are some important differences to keep in mind between JS code running as inline event handlers and normal event handlers. Firstly, it’s possible to
return false;
from the inline event handler, which is equivalent to calling
event.preventDefault()
. Also note that
this
, which is
event.currentTarget
for inline event handlers, would change if you replaced it with an
arrow function
as the event listener.
Outlook
While browser.xhtml contains most parts of the main Firefox UI, some windows and sidebars are based on their own (X)HTML files. Due to the fact that browser.xhtml provides the largest attack vector of our frontend code we focused our initial efforts on securing and hardening browser.xhtml which already drastically improves the status quo to prevent inline script execution. For other windows, such as the “About Firefox” dialog, we go even further by adding CSPs that are much more restrictive and go beyond just blocking scripts. If you are familiar with CSP, by default we set a baseline CSP like
default-src chrome: resource:;
, which basically means we only allow loading resources from files that are shipped with Firefox.
Historically we have already added CSPs to
about:
pages such as
about:preferences
that are displayed like normal websites (cf.
Hardening Firefox against

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同版本和变种的俄罗斯方块游戏设计及其规则差异

不同观点：
• jchw认为Tetris the Grand Master (TGM) 系列的设计比"guideline"或NES Tetris规则更优雅。他指出TGM的旋转和踢墙规则更简洁，而guideline Tetris的踢墙规则过于复杂且允许一些不合理的操作（如T-Spin Triple）。他还提到TGM的随机生成算法较简单且更具挑战性，而7-bag算法生成块的顺序过于规律，降低了游戏的难度和趣味性。

• downsplat回忆早期DOS版本的俄罗斯方块，并提到他编写的各种变体，包括完全随机生成块的版本和一个总是给出最难块的版本。他更倾向于早期版本的随机性，而非现代的简化随机算法。

• qsort提供了现代Tetris游戏的旋转系统规范链接，并指出"guideline"规则（包括Hold、7-bag、多个预览和易于T-spin的旋转系统）使得多人游戏更加有趣，而不仅是谁能最快地堆叠Tetrises。

• throw10920支持墙踢机制的灵活性，认为当用户尝试进行不允许的操作时，系统应尽量提供接近的有用操作，而不是严格遵守操作语义。

• curiouser3提到Apotris（GBA上的Tetris变体）通过各种设置调整控制和灵敏度，使得游戏体验更加出色。

• jstanley质疑在没有长条块的情况下玩100块的可能性，认为这可能是由于其他bug引起的。

• franze分享了自己制作的非Tetris克隆游戏，并表示仍在研究和改进旋转系统。

• zabzonk回忆早期通过调试器修改游戏的经历，包括去除拷贝保护和添加鼠标支持。

• amichail提到他正在开发的游戏DropZap World，结合了Tetris和Candy Crush的元素，并寻求反馈。

• iNic指出在快速游戏环境中，玩家更喜欢"real"旋转系统而非"NES"旋转系统，因为前者允许用更少的按键放置块。

• isolli询问如何向他的儿子介绍Tetris，并寻找适合的当前游戏版本。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术细节，如随机生成算法（7-bag、TGM随机算法）、墙踢机制和旋转系统（SRS）。
• 不同玩家对游戏规则和设计的偏好反映了个人经历和对游戏挑战性的不同期望。
• 争议的焦点在于哪种规则和设计更优越，特别是TGM与guideline Tetris之间的比较。
• 一些评论提到了对早期游戏版本的情感和技术修改，显示了对经典游戏的怀旧和持续探索。

data.title: Ironwood: The first Google TPU for the age of inference
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Google发布了第七代张量处理单元（TPU）——Ironwood，专为推理（inference）设计，是迄今为止最强大、高效的TPU。Ironwood可扩展至9,216个芯片，提供42.5 Exaflops的计算能力，比世界上最强的超级计算机还强大24倍。它配备增强的SparseCore、更大的HBM容量和带宽，以及改进的ICI网络，支持大规模的推理AI模型，如大型语言模型和专家混合模型。Ironwood是Google Cloud AI超算架构的一部分，优化了硬件和软件以应对高要求的AI工作负载，帮助开发者高效处理复杂任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google TPU（张量处理单元）的发布及其影响，包括技术细节、市场竞争、应用场景和可获得性。

不同观点：
• 一些评论质疑TPU是否真的是第一个专门为推理设计的芯片，提到最初的TPU似乎仅用于推理。[nharada]
• 有人对TPU仅存在于云端且难以实际获得表示失望，认为这种硬件的发布缺乏实际意义。[throwaway48476]
• 有人对芯片领域的竞争表示欢迎，认为Google的TPU为Nvidia在机器学习硬件市场上的主导地位带来了挑战。[no_wizard]
• 有人关心这种专用芯片是否会为Google在提供大语言模型服务时带来显著的成本优势，并询问竞争对手是否也能获得类似技术。[nehalem]
• 有人对TPU在架构层面的效率提升来源感兴趣，询问是否依赖于少数大的改进还是许多小的改进。[_hark]
• 有人关注TPU的API支持情况，包括驱动是否已整合进Linux、是否有特定API以及在Google Cloud上的实例如何使用。[tuna74]
• 有评论批评Google在基准测试对比中使用误导性数据，认为不应在不支持fp8的架构之间进行不公平对比，并呼吁更诚实的性能表述。[fancyfredbot]
• 有人询问TPU是否可用于其他用途，如视频编解码或图形处理，并对AI主动生成数据和解释的趋势表示保留态度。[lawlessone]
• 有人希望Google推出类似Coral的本地设备，以满足家庭实验室等本地应用需求。[gigel82]
• 有人认为云资源的普及正在改变市场，尤其是对高级模型的需求增加，导致GPU/加速器的短缺。[DisjointedHunt]
• 有人直接请求Google推出桌面版本的TPU。[ein0p]
• 有人认为Google发布TPU只是为了炫耀，实际上很少出售这些设备。[qoez]
• 有人直接询问是否任何人都可以购买TPU。[wg0]
• 有人关心TPU是否支持CUDA。[DeathArrow]

补充讨论：
• 评论中对TPU的应用场景、性能对比、市场竞争和技术细节（如API支持和架构效率）都有深入讨论。
• 争议焦点之一是Google在基准测试中是否使用了误导性数据来夸大TPU的性能优势。[fancyfredbot]
• 另一个值得注意的点是关于TPU的可获得性和用途的广泛讨论，许多人希望看到更多本地和多样化的应用场景，而不仅仅是云端服务。

Today at Google Cloud Next 25, we’re introducing Ironwood, our seventh-generation Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) — our most performant and scalable custom AI accelerator to date, and the first designed specifically for inference. For more than a decade, TPUs have powered Google’s most demanding AI training and serving workloads, and have enabled our Cloud customers to do the same. Ironwood is our most powerful, capable and energy efficient TPU yet. And it's purpose-built to power thinking, inferential AI models at scale.
Ironwood represents a significant shift in the development of AI and the infrastructure that powers its progress. It’s a move from
responsive
AI models that provide real-time information for people to interpret, to models that provide the
proactive
generation of insights and interpretation. This is what we call the “age of inference” where AI agents will proactively retrieve and generate data to collaboratively deliver insights and answers, not just data.
Ironwood is built to support this next phase of generative AI and its tremendous computational and communication requirements. It scales up to 9,216 liquid cooled chips linked with breakthrough Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI) networking spanning nearly 10 MW. It is one of several new components of
Google Cloud AI Hypercomputer
architecture, which optimizes hardware and software together for the most demanding AI workloads. With Ironwood, developers can also leverage Google’s own
Pathways
software stack to reliably and easily harness the combined computing power of tens of thousands of Ironwood TPUs.
Here’s a closer look at how these innovations work together to take on the most demanding training and serving workloads with unparalleled performance, cost and power efficiency.
Powering the age of inference with Ironwood
Ironwood is designed to gracefully manage the complex computation and communication demands of "thinking models," which encompass Large Language Models (LLMs), Mixture of Experts (MoEs) and advanced reasoning tasks. These models require massive parallel processing and efficient memory access. In particular, Ironwood is designed to minimize data movement and latency on chip while carrying out massive tensor manipulations. At the frontier, the computation demands of thinking models extend well beyond the capacity of any single chip. We designed Ironwood TPUs with a low-latency, high bandwidth ICI network to support coordinated, synchronous communication at full TPU pod scale.
For Google Cloud customers, Ironwood comes in two sizes based on AI workload demands: a 256 chip configuration and a 9,216 chip configuration.

data.title: American Disruption
data.author: shishy
data.article_summary:
文章作者反思了三篇Stratechery上的文章，认为它们在不同方面存在不足。首先，作者讨论了周一发布的关于贸易、关税和科技的文章，认为其缺乏整体框架和令人满意的结论。其次，作者回顾了2023年11月的一篇文章，指出其对特朗普贸易政策的影响预测虽然准确，但表达不够明确。第三篇文章是2021年1月关于互联网3.0和科技历史开端的文章，作者承认其对科技时代转变的预测过早，且误判了转变原因，实际上是美国对世界关闭了大门。

文章进一步探讨了美国制造业的 disruptive（颠覆性）变化，引用克莱顿·克里斯坦森的“颠覆性创新”理论，描述了小公司如何通过满足被忽视的市场需求成功挑战大公司。作者以半导体行业为例，说明制造过程中的低利润环节被外包到亚洲，而创新和利润仍留在美国。然而，随着时间推移，美国在这些关键制造领域的优势逐渐丧失，导致了当前的问题。作者认为，这种 disruptive 过程正是美国制造业面临的核心挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国关税政策的动机和效果

不同观点：
• [mullingitover] 认为关税策略的一部分目的是通过制造股市混乱来压低10年期债券的价格，可能导致美国债务缺乏买家，从而造成破坏性影响。
• [dehrmann] 批评使用贸易流来衡量与各国的经济关系健康状况是错误的，并用三国贸易模型说明贸易逆差并不代表经济问题。
• [morsecodist] 认为讨论关税的好处忽略了核心问题，即关税的真正动机并非提升制造业竞争力或国家安全，而是解决贸易不平衡，且政府的言辞和行动并未表明针对中国的竞争是主要目标。
• [stevenwoo] 质疑文章中使用Uber这种共享经济公司作为制造业讨论的例子，认为不恰当。
• [A_D_E_P_T] 指出当前的贸易政策可能是有意不理性，作为谈判策略的一部分，且当前的政策顺序与合理的回归制造业策略背道而驰。
• [iteratethis]（欧洲视角）认为关税政策没有战略，只是特朗普展示权力的工具，结果是美国对抗全世界，其他国家正在寻找替代方案。
• [eduction] 认为文章基于有缺陷的类比，混淆了基本商业竞争与克莱顿·克里斯坦森提出的颠覆理论。
• [diego_moita] 将当前美国的关税政策比作英国脱欧，认为理性讨论无济于事，个人应设法与混乱局面隔离。
• [torginus] 认为关税政策是为了操纵股市和让亿万富翁受益，是一种骗局。
• [SpicyLemonZest] 强调颠覆理论中的结构性机制，即外包某些制造业能力可能导致美国再也无法有效恢复这些能力，因此关税有其合理性。
• [cess11] 激进地认为特朗普及其亲信是法西斯主义者，关税政策是为了准备战争经济，并清理金融体系中的弱者。
• [throwanem] 认为知名评论员Ben Thompson的观点在当前时代可能不再适用。
• [a3FgH9Lp] 讨论了AI对美国颠覆性创新的加速作用，强调需要主动应对社会影响，并呼吁科技领袖与政策制定者合作制定合理的法规。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于关税政策的真实动机：是为了解决贸易不平衡，还是为了提升制造业竞争力，或仅仅是展示权力和操纵市场。
• 不同评论者对政策制定者的理性程度存在分歧，有人认为政策可能有意不理性，有人则认为讨论这些解释是无关紧要的。
• 讨论还涉及关税政策对全球经济和国际关系的影响，特别是对美国与其他国家的关系。
• 一些评论者关注关税政策对制造业和就业市场的长期影响，并提出应对颠覆性技术（如AI）的策略。

I have a few informal guidelines that govern my writing on Stratechery, including “Don’t post more than one front-page Article a week”, “Don’t talk about my writing process”, and “Don’t start Articles with ‘I’”; it’s an extraordinary week, though, so I’m breaking a few rules.
There are three old Stratechery Articles that, after reflection, missed the mark in different ways.
The most proximate cause for my rule-breaking was Monday’s
Trade, Tariffs, and Tech
; I stand by everything I wrote, but it was incomplete, lacking an overall framework and satisfying conclusion. That’s not surprising given the current uncertainty, but that means I should have waited to publish a front-page Article until I had more clarity (I do much more musing in my Updates, which that Article is now categorized as). Now I have to break my rule and write another Article.
The second Article to revisit is November’s
A Chance to Build
. This Article was in fact deeply pessimistic about President Trump’s promised trade regime, particularly in terms of what it meant for tech; the title and conclusion, however, tried to find some positives. Clearly that was a mistake; that Article was predictive of what was happening, but I obscured the prediction.
The third Article to revisit is January 2021’s
Internet 3.0 and the Beginning of (Tech) History
. This Article was right about tech exiting an economically-defined era — the Aggregation era — and entering a new politically-defined era. It was, however, four years too early, and misdiagnosed the reason for the transition. The driver is not foreign countries closing their doors to America; it’s America closing its door to the world.
The proximate cause of all of this reflection is of course Trump’s disastrous “liberation day” tariffs. The secondary cause is what I wrote about Monday: the U.S. has a genuine problem on its hands thanks to its inability to make things pertinent to modern warfare and high tech. The root cause, however, is very much in Stratechery’s wheelhouse, and worthy of another Article: it’s disruption.
The Disruption of American Manufacturing
The late Professor Clayton Christensen —
one of my personal heroes and inspirations
— coined the term disruption in a seminal paper called
Disruptive Technologies: Catching the Wave
, which he expanded to book-length in
The Innovator’s Dilemma
. However, Christensen’s most concise summary comes from
this 20-year retrospective in Harvard Business Review
:
“Disruption” describes a process whereby a smaller company with fewer resources is able to successfully challenge established incumbent businesses. Specifically, as incumbents focus on improving their products and services for their most demanding (and usually most profitable) customers, they exceed the needs of some segments and ignore the needs of others. Entrants that prove disruptive begin by successfully targeting those overlooked segments, gaining a foothold by delivering more-suitable functionality—frequently at a lower price. Incumbents, chasing higher profitability in more-demanding segments, tend not to respond vigorously. Entrants then move upmarket, delivering the performance that incumbents’ mainstream customers require, while preserving the advantages that drove their early success. When mainstream customers start adopting the entrants’ offerings in volume, disruption has occurred.
This is almost a perfect summary of what has happened in manufacturing, and, as I noted
in that November article
, it started with chips:
That history starts in 1956, when William Shockley founded the Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory to commercialize the transistor that he had helped invent at Bell Labs; he chose Mountain View to be close to his ailing mother. A year later the so-called “Traitorous Eight”, led by Robert Noyce, left and founded Fairchild Semiconductor down the road. Six years after that Fairchild Semiconductor opened a facility in Hong Kong to assemble and test semiconductors. Assembly required manually attaching wires to a semiconductor chip, a labor-intensive and monotonous task that was difficult to do economically with American wages, which ran about $2.50/hour; Hong Kong wages were a tenth of that. Four years later Texas Instruments opened a facility in Taiwan, where wages were $0.19/hour; two years after that Fairchild Semiconductor opened another facility in Singapore, where wages were $0.11/hour.
In other words, you can make the case that the classic story of Silicon Valley isn’t completely honest. Chips did have marginal costs, but that marginal cost was, within single digit years of the founding of Silicon Valley, exported to Asia.
Notice what did still happen in the United States, at least back then: actual chip fabrication.

文章作者反思了三篇Stratechery上的文章，认为它们在不同方面存在不足。首先，作者讨论了周一发布的关于贸易、关税和科技的文章，认为其缺乏整体框架和令人满意的结论。其次，作者回顾了2023年11月的一篇文章，指出其对特朗普贸易政策的影响预测虽然准确，但表达不够明确。第三篇文章是2021年1月关于互联网3.0和科技历史开端的文章，作者承认其对科技时代转变的预测过早，且误判了转变原因，实际上是美国对世界关闭了大门。

文章进一步探讨了美国制造业的 disruptive（颠覆性）变化，引用克莱顿·克里斯坦森的“颠覆性创新”理论，描述了小公司如何通过满足被忽视的市场需求成功挑战大公司。作者以半导体行业为例，说明制造过程中的低利润环节被外包到亚洲，而创新和利润仍留在美国。然而，随着时间推移，美国在这些关键制造领域的优势逐渐丧失，导致了当前的问题。作者认为，这种 disruptive 过程正是美国制造业面临的核心挑战。

主要讨论点：音频录制设备和麦克风对录音质量的影响

不同观点：
• MrJagil认为音频录制设备对录音质量有重要影响，并提到Zoom F3是新的主力设备，Sony PCM D100则是已停产的经典设备。他表示这些设备在行业内被广泛认可，说明专业人士能够辨别音质好坏。

• kazinator指出，该比较仅针对录音硬件设备，而非麦克风。他提到，虽然有一些使用不同麦克风录制的音频样本，但并没有对麦克风进行量化比较，仅对录音设备进行了定量分析。

• pier25表示，虽然该资源非常有用，但录音中的噪音主要来源于麦克风本身。他以Rode NT1麦克风为例，指出在录制非常安静的音源时，没有听到来自前置放大器的任何噪音。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于录音质量的关键因素。MrJagil强调录音设备的作用，而pier25则认为麦克风对噪音的影响更大。

• kazinator的评论提醒读者注意比较的对象，强调了区分录音设备和麦克风的重要性，以避免混淆两者对音质的影响。

• pier25的实际使用经验为讨论提供了具体的例子，强调了麦克风选择在减少噪音方面的重要性。

data.title: An LLM Query Understanding Service
data.author: softwaredoug
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了如何利用LLM（大语言模型）快速改进搜索功能，将复杂查询分解为关键维度，从而实现结构化搜索。作者提到，使用简单的LLM可以在几天内完成以往需要数月的工作，且无需依赖OpenAI或Gemini等外部服务，可以通过本地基础设施运行LLM，提高速度并降低成本。

文章详细描述了如何通过FastAPI部署一个调用LLM的应用，并以Qwen2-7B模型为例展示了如何使用PyTorch调用轻量级LLM。此外，文章还介绍了如何创建Docker镜像，并将其部署到Google Kubernetes Engine（GKE）的自动驾驶模式中。

最后，文章提醒了可能遇到的节点分配问题及相应的Kubernetes操作步骤，如查看和描述pod状态，确保正确分配GPU资源。如果配额不足，可能会导致pod无法分配到合适的节点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用大型语言模型（LLM）将搜索查询转换为结构化搜索过滤器的技巧及其技术细节

不同观点：
• simonw: 通过在多个LLM上测试，如Gemini 1.5 Flash 8B、Llama 3.2 3B和deepseek-r1:1.5b，发现不同模型在处理结构化搜索过滤器时的表现各异。Gemini 1.5 Flash 8B表现良好且成本低廉，Llama 3.2 3B作为本地小模型也能胜任，而deepseek-r1:1.5b则给出了错误答案。所有测试均通过llm.datasette.io平台及相关插件完成。

• MarkSweep: 建议使用LLM API的“结构化输出”功能，以提高生成有效JSON并符合预期架构的可能性。提供了相关API文档链接，如Gemini API和Ollama API，以帮助实现这一功能。

补充讨论：
• hamelsmu: 赞赏Doug在搜索领域的贡献，提到其著作《Relevant Search》并对其重新教授相关知识表示高兴。这一评论更侧重于对Doug个人的认可和对相关知识传播的支持。

争议焦点：
• 不同LLM模型在处理结构化数据时的性能差异，尤其是deepseek-r1:1.5b给出了错误答案，这表明在选择模型时需考虑其准确性和可靠性。
• 是否采用LLM API的“结构化输出”功能以提高JSON输出的有效性，这涉及技术实现的选择和优化。

总结：讨论主要围绕如何利用LLM将搜索查询转换为结构化过滤器以及各模型的表现差异，同时提出了技术优化建议和相关知识的传播。

We need to be cheating at search with LLMs. Indeed
I’m teaching a whole course on this in July
.
With an LLM we can implement in days what previously took months. We can take apart a query like “brown leather sofa” into the important dimensions of intent — “color: brown, material: leather, category:couches” etc. With this power
all search is structured now
.
Even better we can do this all without calling out to OpenAI/Gemini/…. We can use simple LLMs running in
our infrastructure
making it faster and cheaper.
I’m going to show you how. Let’s get started. Follow along
in this repo
.
The service - wrapping an open source LLM

The Docker Image
To create a kubernetes pod, we need a Docker image with our app. One dependency is a headache with Docker - PyTorch.  Luckily someone has written a great article on
shrinking pytorch images
, which is a great starting point for
our Dockerfile
.
OK now to build and upload to GCR  - Google’s Container Registry - so our pod can pull the container. There’s a handy
scripts/publish_gcp.sh
script in the repo. I recommend running that script if you’re getting started, as it executes the steps in this article.
We build an amd64 image and publish it:
PLATFORM
=
"linux/amd64"
GCP_PROJECT_ID
=
$(
gcloud config get-value project
)
docker buildx build
--platform
$PLATFORM
-t
"gcr.io/
$GCP_PROJECT_ID
/fastapi-gke:latest"
.
docker push
"gcr.io/
$GCP_PROJECT_ID
/fastapi-gke:latest"
Setting up GKE autopilot mode
If you have a Google Cloud account, create a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with default settings. Now you have an autopilot cluster! Congrats you know Kubernetes 🎉.
(If you don’t have a Google Cloud account, you can
create one and get $300 of credits
)
Normally with kubernetes, you’d manually allocate nodes to your cluster. GKE’s Autopilot does this for you, though may take a few minutes to spin up a VM as it finds compute for you.
With that in mind, let’s look at my kubernetes deployment (
source here
)
The first part here sets up a deployment of the image
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
name: llm-query-understand
namespace: softwaredoug-training
spec:
replicas: 1
selector:
matchLabels:
app: llm-query-understand
template:
metadata:
labels:
app: llm-query-understand
spec:
containers:
- name: fastapi
image: gcr.io/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/fastapi-gke:latest
# <- what we just pushed up to GCR
ports:
- containerPort: 80
# <- expose port 80
Then, adding the needed resources:
resources:
requests:
memory:
"32Gi"
cpu:
"2"
nvidia.com/gpu:
"1"
limits:
memory:
"32Gi"
cpu:
"2"
nvidia.com/gpu:
"1"
OK good enough - we want a machine with 32 GB RAM, 2 CPUs, and a single GPU.
Finally to ensure we are scheduled correctly, we need some
node selectors specific to GKE
:
nodeSelector:
# Ensure your GPU quotas allow you to have a compute
# instance with a GPU
cloud.google.com/compute-class:
"Accelerator"
cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator-count:
"1"
cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator:
"nvidia-l4"

• MarkSweep: 建议使用LLM API的“结构化输出”功能，以提高生成有效JSON并符合预期架构的可能性。提供了相关API文档链接，如Gemini API和Ollama API，以帮助实现这一功能。

补充讨论：
• hamelsmu: 赞赏Doug在搜索领域的贡献，提到其著作《Relevant Search》并对其重新教授相关知识表示高兴。这一评论更侧重于对Doug个人的认可和对相关知识传播的支持。

争议焦点：
• 不同LLM模型在处理结构化数据时的性能差异，尤其是deepseek-r1:1.5b给出了错误答案，这表明在选择模型时需考虑其准确性和可靠性。
• 是否采用LLM API的“结构化输出”功能以提高JSON输出的有效性，这涉及技术实现的选择和优化。

总结：讨论主要围绕如何利用LLM将搜索查询转换为结构化过滤器以及各模型的表现差异，同时提出了技术优化建议和相关知识的传播。

data.title: Show HN: Webtor – open-source torrent streaming engine
data.author: vintikzzzz
data.article_summary: Webtor.io 是一个在线工具，允许用户通过三个简单步骤将种子文件或磁力链接转换为直接下载链接，而无需使用种子客户端。用户可以上传种子文件并获取下载链接，支持选择性文件下载、视频和音频在线流媒体播放，且无大小限制。它还提供 Chrome 扩展，支持将种子打包为 ZIP 档案下载，并具备开发者友好的 SDK。Webtor.io 通过 HTTPS 协议传输数据，用户无需开启 VPN，下载行为对 ISP 不可见，确保匿名和安全。该服务提供 7 天免费试用，支持移动设备使用，所有组件均为开源，遵循 MIT 许可证。

data.title: Visual Reasoning Is Coming Soon
data.author: softwaredoug
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了OpenAI最新发布的GPT-4o模型在图像生成和处理方面的突破，特别是其在视觉推理（visual reasoning）上的潜力。过去，多模态大语言模型在处理图像时存在缺陷，模型只能通过文本描述生成图像，导致结果往往与预期不符。而GPT-4o模型能够保留对话的完整上下文，直接生成更一致的图像，解决了这一问题。例如，它可以根据用户提供的猫的照片，准确地给这只猫戴上侦探帽和单片眼镜。

文章还展望了这一技术在实际应用中的广泛可能性，如将手绘图转化为精美的信息图、编辑假期照片、虚拟试衣等。最重要的是，文章预测视觉推理将成为未来的真正创新，模型将能够通过视觉化场景和推理来解决现实问题。文章最后通过一个"杯子中的弹珠"问题演示了视觉推理的潜在应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频生成模型及其在视觉推理和图像处理中的应用与局限

不同观点：
• AIPedant认为，视频生成模型在物理和空间推理任务上存在局限，尤其是对于物体恒存性和物理常识的理解。即便如DeepMind的Veo2这样先进的模型也存在这些问题。同时指出，人类和脊椎动物通过观察学习这些概念，而Transformer模型即使在大量数据训练下可能也无法 robustly 掌握这些能力。
• nkingsy指出，当前的图像生成技术在编辑图像时，无法精准地保留原图特征，生成结果往往是改变了整体外观，比如生成更年轻、更完美的猫，而在编辑人像时，结果显得怪异。
• Tiberium认为，4o的图像生成特征在编辑图像时改变了整个图像，而Gemini 2.0 Flash在保留未编辑部分的表现更好，建议使用或提及更先进的图像生成工具。
• porphyra提出，人类通过视频而不是静止图像来理解世界，因为视频提供了因果关系和三维结构的信息，而目前的模型仅通过静止图像训练，因此在理解事物相互影响上存在困难。
• District5524澄清，传统LLM在图像生成中的作用很小，主要是扩散模型在起作用，并提供了相关技术文档支持这一观点。
• CSMastermind认为，许多模型的进展是显而易见的下一步，但细节上仍有非显而易见的创新。
• rel_ic对博客文章的乐观语气与终结者机器人图片的不一致感到不解，质疑作者的认真性。
• anxoo指出，当前的模型在视觉推理任务上表现不一，某些模型在处理物理问题时表现较好，但作者未能充分证明“视觉推理”的概念。
• KTibow提到，有人猜测o3模型已经使用了视觉推理，并因此取得了突破。

补充讨论：
• 对不同图像生成工具和模型在处理和编辑图像时的表现进行了比较，特别是4o和Gemini 2.0 Flash。
• 讨论了人类和模型在学习物理概念上的差异，强调了观察和训练数据对模型能力的影响。
• 对视觉推理和图像生成的技术细节和应用场景进行了探讨，包括合成数据和真实数据的使用。
• 对当前模型进展的评价存在争议，有人认为进展显著，有人则质疑具体成果和概念的合理性。

43633568.article_content:
Visual Reasoning is Coming Soon
I gotta say –
I love it living in exponential times
. I can just wish that something existed and then within a month it does! This time it happened with
OpenAI's 4o image generation release
. In this blog post I'll briefly cover the release and why I think it's pretty cool. Then I'll dive into a new opportunity that I think is even more exciting –
visual reasoning
.
Rather watch than read?
Hey, I get it - sometimes you just want to kick back and watch! Check out this quick video where I walk through everything in this post. Same great content, just easier on the eyes!
Why Image Manipulation with LLMs Stinks
Working with images in Multimodal LLMs has been a mostly one-sided affair. On one hand, it's really cool that you can drop an image into an LLM conversation and get the model to reason about it. But when you ask the model to generate an image, there is a disconnect, because all the model can do is describe the image in text and then call out to an external image generation tool to generate the image based on that text. Text is a poor communication medium for images, and the resulting image is often quite disconnected from the expected result because the short description that the LLM provides to the image generation tool will rarely capture the full context of the conversation.
The problem is most pronounced when attempting to go back and forth working on an idea for an image. You can show the LLM an image of your cat and then say "make this cat wear a detective hat and a monocle". The best the model can do is to put a detective hat and monocle on
some
cat, not the one in your image. To make matters worse, the model can't even see the image that it has just created. So if you ask for a modification to first generation attempt, then the subsequent generations are really just starting over from scratch and hoping that a more detailed description to the image generation tool will make things better... it won't.
Left: OpenAI's pet cat. Right: The best a traditional LLM can do when asked to give it a detective hat and monocle.
OpenAI's Release Brings True Image Manipulation to LLMs
OpenAI's image generation release changes all of this. OpenAI's newest GPT-4o model carries the full context of the conversation into the image generation, and rather than call out to an external model, it is the very same GPT-4o model that does the image generation. By carrying the full context of the conversation –
including the previous images
– into the generation of the new image you can generate much more consistent imagery.
Thus, stealing OpenAI's example, you can show it a photo of your cat, tell it to give
your cat
a detective hat, et voila! It works!
Left: OpenAI's pet cat. Right: GPT-4o's generation when asked to give the same cat a detective hat and monocle. Much more consistent!
Now if all we could do with this technology is stick silly costumes on our cats, then this would honestly be a pretty lame achievement. But think about what we're angling for here. You'll be able to turn hand-drawn garbage into sophisticated infographics and marketing material. You'll be able to take crappy matplotlib charts and reformat them as professional-looking plots that go into slides. You'll be able to try on clothes virtually before you buy them. You'll be able to create photo collages from your photos, game assets, and 3D models. You'll be able to edit your vacation photos to remove that one person who blinked. You'll be able to take a photo of your living room and try out different furniture arrangements and color schemes. You'll be able to take a photo of your garden and get suggestions for where to plant new flowers. The possibilities are endless when you can manipulate images with the full context of a conversation.
Visual Reasoning will be the Real Innovation
All of the above is but prologue for what will come next. Models perform better when they take time to reason. This is because models have no internal monologue. Whereas humans pause and think about a question prior to answering, models have to generate tokens in order to think. But to this point models have only been able to reason in the space of words, and words are ill-suited for reasoning through many types of real world problems. But soon the models' new image manipulation capabilities will power a new form of reasoning. Right now, this ability is mostly useful for image editing. Soon, models will have the ability to visualize different scenarios and visually reason about the world around them.
Demoing Visual Reasoning
Let's try out an example right now and get a glimpse of how visual reasoning will work. For our experiment we'll use
Matthew Berman's marble in a cup problem
– it's one of his go-to reasoning challenges when playing around with a new model:
I've put a marble in a glass. The glass is then turned upside down and put on a table. Then the glass is picked up and put into the microwave. Where is the marble?
It's a great problem

• nkingsy指出，当前的图像生成技术在编辑图像时，无法精准地保留原图特征，生成结果往往是改变了整体外观，比如生成更年轻、更完美的猫，而在编辑人像时，结果显得怪异。
• Tiberium认为，4o的图像生成特征在编辑图像时改变了整个图像，而Gemini 2.0 Flash在保留未编辑部分的表现更好，建议使用或提及更先进的图像生成工具。
• porphyra提出，人类通过视频而不是静止图像来理解世界，因为视频提供了因果关系和三维结构的信息，而目前的模型仅通过静止图像训练，因此在理解事物相互影响上存在困难。
• District5524澄清，传统LLM在图像生成中的作用很小，主要是扩散模型在起作用，并提供了相关技术文档支持这一观点。
• CSMastermind认为，许多模型的进展是显而易见的下一步，但细节上仍有非显而易见的创新。
• rel_ic对博客文章的乐观语气与终结者机器人图片的不一致感到不解，质疑作者的认真性。
• anxoo指出，当前的模型在视觉推理任务上表现不一，某些模型在处理物理问题时表现较好，但作者未能充分证明“视觉推理”的概念。
• KTibow提到，有人猜测o3模型已经使用了视觉推理，并因此取得了突破。

补充讨论：
• 对不同图像生成工具和模型在处理和编辑图像时的表现进行了比较，特别是4o和Gemini 2.0 Flash。
• 讨论了人类和模型在学习物理概念上的差异，强调了观察和训练数据对模型能力的影响。
• 对视觉推理和图像生成的技术细节和应用场景进行了探讨，包括合成数据和真实数据的使用。
• 对当前模型进展的评价存在争议，有人认为进展显著，有人则质疑具体成果和概念的合理性。

43635295.article_content:
GPD Pocket 4 Speaker DSP
Configuring PipeWire to make laptop speakers sound better (Bankstown, Convolution/FIR, etc.)
By
Manawyrm (
@manawyrm@chaos.social
)
|
Sunday, April 06, 2025
Result
Motivation
Modern speakers require a lot of DSP magic to sound as good as they do.
Speakers traditionally needed to be built very carefully to achieve a very flat frequency response and as few artifacts as possible.
These days, many mobile devices like phones, laptops, etc. do a lot of digital signal processing in software in order to make tiny speakers output a lot of sound.
Many different tricks are used, such as
psycho-acoustic bass enhancement
, limiters (allowing for higher power peaks) and
volume-dependent equalization
(frequency response of human hearing is very volume-dependent).
The Asahi Linux project (Linux on Apple Silicon MacBooks) has done a lot of work to make MacBooks sound as good as possible on Linux:
AsahiLinux/asahi-audio: Userspace audio for Asahi Linux
How?
Using
Room EQ Wizard
the frequency/impulse response of the built-in speakers was measured.
Even with very suboptimal measurement equipment (cheap microphone, questionable audio interface), we can clearly see the sloped bass response (expected with speakers of this size) and then also a very noticeable peak/resonance at ~4kHz.
This peak is very audible and leads to a harsh, distorted sound when listening to music.
REW can do arithmetic operations on the curves, so after generating a filter curve for a 300Hz slope, both channels were divided (A/B) against that curve and then inverted (1/A) and exported as a .wav impulse response.
That impulse response .wav file can then be used in a convolution DSP filter.
The DSP configuration/pipeline of a 14" MacBook Pro was then used as a template, the multi-speaker setup (modern MacBooks have 6 speakers!) was stripped-down to just a single stereo pair and the parameters were changed a bit.
The impulse response .wav was (of course) replaced with our newly generated REW output.

Room EQ Wizard

data.title: Show HN: I built an app to generate story relationships using Mermaidjs
data.author: herol3oy
data.article_summary: Austen是一个由AI驱动的Angular应用，利用Analogjs构建，旨在通过Mermaidjs图表展示书籍角色的关系。其主要功能包括从Open Library搜索和分析书籍、AI分析角色关系、生成Mermaid图表、保存、下载（SVG、PNG）和管理图表、分享或私密保存图表，以及查看其他用户公开的图表。技术栈包括Angular、Analog、TypeScript、Supabase、Cloudflare Pages等。用户可以克隆项目、安装依赖、配置环境变量并启动开发服务器来使用该应用。未来计划增加图表点赞功能和加载更多图表的选项。项目遵循MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自动生成书籍角色关系图的工具及其效果和应用

不同观点：
• skeptrune: 测试了《The Wise Man's Fear》和《Harry Potter》，结果不尽如人意，尤其是角色关系展示不够准确。他更关注如何利用这些图表生成结构化的JSON对象，以改进搜索和推荐功能。
• eterps: 认为如果系统能通过任意epub文件自动生成关系图，而无需完整阅读书籍，将更有趣。建议使用aichat和graphviz实现这一功能。
• rmnclmnt: 测试了《Time Out of Joint》，系统仅正确识别了故事的前半部分，未涉及剧透。
• memhole: 提供链接供用户查看工具的准确性，指出准确率大约在60%左右。
• febed: 利用MermaidJS与LLM结合，成功绘制业务逻辑的流程图，帮助发现了一些极端情况。
• kretaceous: 测试了《Circe》，发现角色关系错误，如将Circe描述为Helios的女儿，但同时又有其他矛盾的关系。
• iddan: 建议将《Pride and Prejudice》加入示例中。
• herol3oy: 工具的开发者，回应了评论，承认结果可能不够简洁或准确，解释了由于预算限制，只能使用较便宜的语言模型服务，如DeepSeek。
• maxwellg: 认为工具对参考书籍的概述功能有趣，甚至可以将数据库事务视为角色关系。
• kacesensitive: 测试了《Dungeon Crawler Carl》，结果错误且有趣，提供了错误的关系图示例。
• blancotech: 认为结果不够全面，相比之下，ChatGPT结合网络搜索功能，通过简单提示生成关系图效果更好。
• knowitnone: 认为工具很有用，特别是在需要回顾角色身份时。
• wduquette: 质疑这种故事关系图是否常见，或者工具的开发者是否独创了这一工具和图示。
• napoleongl: 提到曾幻想使用mermaid生成电视剧情和角色的关系图。
• aardvark179: 测试了《Book of the New Sun》，系统未能正确识别重要角色Dorcas，且将一把剑识别为角色的同伴。

补充讨论：
• 工具的准确性和全面性是用户主要关心的问题，尤其是对复杂书籍和角色的处理能力。
• 用户对如何改进工具提出了不同建议，包括使用更好的语言模型和自动化生成图表的方法。
• 争议焦点在于工具生成的关系图的可靠性和实用性，部分用户认为结果不够准确或全面。
• 开发者回应了用户的反馈，解释了技术限制和预算问题，并表示会继续改进工具。

Austen
Austen is an AI-powered Angular application initialized with Analogjs to generate story relationships between book characters using Mermaidjs diagrams.

📚 Search and analyze any book from Open Library
🤖 AI-powered character relationship analysis
📊 Generate Mermaid diagrams
💾 Save, download (SVG, PNG) and manage your generated graphs
🌐 Share graphs publicly or keep them private
🔍 Discover public graphs generated by other users

data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了作者参与的Prospero挑战，该挑战要求渲染莎士比亚《暴风雨》中的一段引文，输入是一个包含7866个操作的数学公式，每个像素都需要评估该公式。作者尝试了多种方法来加速执行，包括添加窥孔优化和实现"仅保留结果符号"的优化，后者效果显著。

作者首先实现了一个简单的SSA形式解释器，作为基准。该解释器将操作名和索引对应，避免运行时字典查找，并按顺序执行操作。然而，这种方法非常慢，因为需要执行大量的浮点运算。

为了优化，作者借鉴了Matt的quadtree方法，通过递归地将图像分成四个象限，并对每个象限进行范围分析，从而显著缩小公式规模。经过几层递归后，公式往往只剩下几百甚至几十个操作，大大提升了渲染速度。

最终，作者在RPython中进行原型设计，并为了性能提升用C重写了程序。所有代码已发布在Github上。

Recently I had a lot of fun playing with the
Prospero
Challenge
by
Matt
Keeter
. The challenge is to render a 1024x1024 image of
a quote from The Tempest by Shakespeare. The input is a mathematical formula
with 7866 operations, which is evaluated once per pixel.
What made the challenge particularly enticing for me personally was the fact
that the formula is basically a trace in
SSA-form
– a
linear sequence of operations, where every variable is assigned exactly once.
The challenge is to evaluate the formula as fast as possible. I tried a number
of ideas how to speed up execution and will talk about them in this somewhat
meandering post. Most of it follows Matt's implementation
Fidget
very closely. There are two points
of difference:
I tried to add more peephole optimizations, but they didn't end up helping
much.
I implemented a "demanded information" optimization that removes a lot of
operations by only keeping the sign of the result. This optimization ended up
being useful.
Most of the prototyping in this post was done in RPython (a statically typable
subset of Python2, that can be compiled to C), but I later rewrote the program
in C to get better performance. All the code
can be found on
Github
.
Input program
¶
The input program is a sequence of operations, like this:

The first column is the name of the result variable, the second column is the
operation, and the rest are the arguments to the operation.
var-x
is a
special operation that returns the x-coordinate of the pixel being rendered,
and equivalently for
var-y
the y-coordinate. The sign of the result gives the
color of the pixel, the absolute value is not important.
A baseline interpreter
¶
To run the program, I first parse them and replace the register names with
indexes, to avoid any dictionary lookups at runtime.
Then I implemented a simple interpreter for the SSA-form
input program. The interpreter is a simple register machine, where every
operation is executed in order. The result of the operation is stored into a
list of results, and the next operation is executed. This was the slow baseline
implementation of the interpreter but it's very useful to compare against the optimized
versions.

it performs 7866 * 1024 * 1024 float operations, plus the interpretation overhead.
Using Quadtrees to render the picture
¶
The approach that Matt describes in his really excellent
talk
is to use
quadtrees
: recursively subdivide the
image into quadrants, and evaluate the formula in each quadrant. For every
quadrant you can simplify the formula by doing a range analysis. After a few
recursion steps, the formula becomes significantly smaller, often only a few
hundred or a few dozen operations.

data.title: Show HN: Fermi – A Wordle-style game for order-of-magnitude thinking
data.author: andrewrn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个基于费米估算的游戏设计及其用户界面和用户体验问题

不同观点：
• [beeftime] 认为需要手动选择和调整因素，而不是默认提供所有因素。建议像Wordle一样有锁定赢/输状态，并允许增加/减少因素的量级和运算顺序。对当前滑块默认设置导致胜利表示不满。
• [jy14898] 质疑因素的可排序性和可选择性，指出乘法交换律（axb = bxa），并怀疑因素选择的合理性。
• [thatnerd] 指出单位错误，建议增加单位取消检查功能，并希望在方程中选择乘法或除法。
• [zamadatix] 建议增加“普通”和“困难”模式，普通模式提供因素名称，困难模式需要自己提出因素名称和值。提出赢的条件和“超级”赢的建议。
• [bangaladore] 对游戏机制感到困惑，建议默认包含所有因素，并允许减少使用因素。对猜测后的反馈不清表示不满，希望有更明确的提示和比较信息。
• [iterance] 对游戏中的范围和量级问题提出疑问，指出费米问题的目标是达到合适的量级，而非游戏中提供的预设范围。
• [hallh] 认为游戏有潜力但需要打磨，对因素的明显性和滑块的范围限制表示失望，建议更多不相关因素的估算。
• [whiterook6] 在手机上遇到界面问题，无法理解如何选择和操作因素及滑块，整体用户体验混乱。
• [crmi] 喜欢概念但认为UI confusing，建议不提供预设范围以增加难度，并提出逐步提示和分享结果的建议。
• [mncharity] 强调界限而非点估计，建议多重推理链和自我评估机制，以提升费米估算的游戏性。
• [bobdigit] 建议开发针对儿童/年轻观众的版本。
• [mNovak] 认为滑块范围太窄，失去费米估算的乐趣，建议更宽的量级范围和粗略的估算方式。
• [mrngm] 建议简化初始教程，直接展示问题，调整滑块以适应量级思维，并提出多种滑块策略和用户选择方案。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的核心争议在于滑块的默认设置和范围，以及是否应该提供所有因素。部分玩家认为默认设置和预设范围降低了游戏的挑战性和趣味性。
• 用户界面的复杂性和不明确的反馈机制是另一个主要问题，许多玩家在操作和理解游戏机制上遇到了困难。
• 多种模式和不同难度级别的建议被提出，以增加游戏的深度和可玩性。
• 一些玩家对单位错误和缺乏明确的单位取消检查功能表示不满，希望有更严谨的数学机制。
• 总体而言，玩家对游戏的概念表示认可，但对其执行和用户体验方面提出了诸多改进建议。

data.title: Rolex Caliber 7135: new indirect impulse escapement and high frequency movement
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary: Rolex推出了全新表款Land-Dweller，这是多年来最具意义的新品。该表款采用全新设计的Dynapulse escapement，这是一种专利间接脉冲擒纵机构，使用双硅轮，是品牌首个机械高频机芯（Caliber 7135）。表壳设计灵感源于1970年代的Ref. 1530和Oysterquartz型号，但更薄，提供36毫米和40毫米表径选择。新款配备五排Flat Jubilee表链和Crownclasp隐藏式表扣。表壳材质包括钢、Everose金和铂金，部分款式镶嵌钻石。表盘设计融合现有款式元素，采用蜂窝图案和探险家系列的数字时标。背透设计展示独特的Dynapulse擒纵机构，旨在提高精度并减少摩擦，从而延长保养间隔。

43633005.article_content:
No April Fool's, here it is, the Rolex Land-Dweller, what might be the most meaningful release from Rolex in years. Punctuating the top Swiss brand's manufacturing and industrial expertise, it's an entirely new model that draws on some vintage design inspiration but is highlighted by the Dynapulse escapement — a proprietary, patented, and industrially optimized indirect impulse escapement using dual silicon wheels. The caliber 7135 inside is officially the brand's first mechanical high frequency movement. It has a new steel case that recalls the ref. 1530 and Oysterquartz models from the 1970s but is 20% thinner than a Datejust. It vaults Rolex back into the integrated bracelet sportswatch arena with a movement that achieves a host of technical firsts and marks a great leap forward in its ongoing quest for precision.
With every patent filed or trademark applied for, Rolex sets a certain corner of the internet on fire. On July 28th, 2023, the name "Land-Dweller" was trademarked (alongside "Coast-Dweller") by Rolex U.S.A. Shortly thereafter, watch internet sleuths broadcast the news via posts, reels, shorts, TikToks, you name it. Posts were shared, emojis were added, and within days, all of this blew over. Today, Rolex takes advantage of that sneaky summer of 2023 trademark.
If you're a vintage Rolex enthusiast, this case shape and integrated bracelet should look familiar. Commonly referred to as the "Oysterquartz" design, this shape was first introduced with the mechanical Datejust ref. 1530 in 1975 — exactly 50 years ago. The successor Oysterquartz references 17000 (Datejust) and 19018 (Day-Date) began production in 1977, popularizing the design, hence the name.
Rolex Datejust Ref. 1530 (1975)
Rolex Datejust Oysterquartz Ref. 17013 (1977)
The new-for-2025 Land-Dweller revives the 50-year-old ref. 1530 shape with slight proportional tweaks measuring 36mm or 40mm in diameter and 9.70mm thick — 2.3mm thinner than the standard Datejust 41. The distinctive five-row Flat Jubilee bracelet found on many of these vintage references has been updated for the Land-Dweller. Most notable is the inclusion of a Crownclasp — Rolex's term for a "hidden" clasp featuring a crown-shaped pull, a feature not offered on the Datejust 36 and 41 Jubilee since 2018. Case metal options presented today are steel with a white gold fluted bezel, Everose gold with or without a baguette diamond-set bezel, and platinum with or without a baguette diamond-set bezel.
Dial-wise, the Land-Dweller is a mix of existing Rolex models with a bit of Datejust feel to the dial, albeit with a new honeycomb motif treatment and applied cardinal numerals in the style of the Explorer collection as well as the Cyclops on the crystal to magnify the date.
On the backside is an exhibition caseback. Here's why.
The Rolex Dynapulse Escapement
The Land-Dweller is fitted with a brand new and patented indirect impulse escapement, which Rolex is calling the Dynapulse escapement. As an idea, this type of escapement tech dates back to the mid to late 1700s with Pierre Le Roy, John Arnold, and Thomas Earnshaw and has been refined by many great watchmakers since. Today, Rolex presents its own iteration of the centuries-old and theoretically superior direct impulse escapement.
Swiss Lever Escapement
In practice, the lever escapement is king. If you own a mechanical watch, there is a very high probability it utilizes the lever, from Seiko 5s to every prior Rolex ever made. The Crown introduced a proprietary lever escapement in 2015 — the Chronergy escapement. Even with ultra-optimized geometry like in the Chronergy system, any lever escapement has a few fundamental flaws. The most significant of which is the lever's inherent friction and, therefore, need for lubrication. Just by glancing at the lever escapement in action, the friction between the escape wheel teeth and ruby pallets is quite evident. The teeth are scraping along the jewels. At 28,800 vph (4 Hz), this collision happens eight times per second or 252,288,000 times per year. Oil is used to combat this friction, and this is the reason you need your watch serviced every few years.
Rolex Chronergy Escapement
Direct impulse escapements have none of this scraping action as the force, or impulse, is delivered, you guessed it, directly from the escape wheel(s) to the balance. Beyond longer service intervals, direct impulse escapements are more efficient and provide a more consistent rate over time when compared to the lever. These advantages make for a more accurate watch. The natural, detent (or chronometer), and coaxial are all categorically direct impulse escapements.
If this category of escapements is technically superior, why doesn't everyone use them then? Nothing is perfect, especially in watchmaking, and direct impulse escapements are no different. data.author: bookofjoe

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：维生素D补充剂对急性呼吸道感染（ARI）及总体健康的影响

不同观点：
• [seizethecheese] 认为根据荟萃分析，维生素D与安慰剂相比在降低总体ARI风险方面没有统计学上的显著影响，因为p值略微超过0.05的显著性水平。因此，声称维生素D有效预防ARI没有足够支持。
• [brokegrammer] 支持上述观点，明确指出该研究结论是维生素D补充剂无助于预防急性呼吸道感染。
• [johnisgood] 提到尽管有阳光暴露或补充维生素D，维生素D缺乏仍然可能存在，建议进行检测以确保维生素D水平正常。同时分享了个人补充维生素D的经历。
• [normalaccess] 引用了Steve Gibson和Dr. John Campbell的资源，强调了维生素D代谢产物（如calcifediol）在感染后治疗中的潜在作用，而非单纯依赖维生素D补充剂。
• [bmacho] 提出疑问，既然低维生素D水平与流感相关，但补充维生素D没有帮助，是否意味着有其他因素在起作用。
• [rwbt] 关注自然饮食中富含维生素D的食物，除了补充剂外，询问其他获取维生素D的途径。
• [mrandish] 提供了一个综合观点，认为补充维生素D对预防上呼吸道感染效果不明显，但维生素D缺乏可能与感染的严重程度有关。补充维生素D在缺乏时是有意义的，但过量补充可能有害。

补充讨论：
• [gnabgib] 提供了一些相关讨论的链接，涉及到高剂量维生素D对多发性硬化症和COVID-19的影响，但这些讨论在当前评论中没有详细展开。
• [moltar] 推荐使用dminder应用来监测维生素D的摄入量，包括阳光和补充剂的来源。

争议焦点：
• 维生素D补充剂是否能有效预防急性呼吸道感染。
• 维生素D缺乏与感染严重程度之间的关系是否足以支持普遍补充维生素D。
• 补充维生素D的最佳时机和剂量，以及过量补充的潜在风险。

总结：讨论围绕维生素D补充剂在预防和治疗呼吸道感染中的作用展开，不同观点集中在维生素D的效果、缺乏的检测与补充、以及过量补充的风险。讨论还涉及到维生素D代谢产物在感染治疗中的潜在重要性。

data.article_summary: LispE是一款由Naver开发的现代Lisp方言，通过引入**defpat**、**defmacro**和**defpred**等创新结构，扩展了传统Lisp的功能，特别是在模式匹配和逻辑编程方面。与Common Lisp、Scheme和Clojure不同，LispE的**defpat**允许在函数定义中使用模式匹配，根据不同参数模式定义多个同名函数，实现声明式的多态处理。例如，FizzBuzz问题中，LispE可以通过模式匹配简洁地处理不同条件，而无需手动编写逻辑。同时，**defpat**还支持Kleene操作符（`+`, `*`, `%`），可以轻松匹配序列模式。相比之下，其他Lisp方言需要手动实现循环和条件逻辑，代码更为复杂。LispE通过这些特性提供了更强大的模式匹配和序列处理能力。

Exploring LispE: A Distinctive Take on Lisp Through Pattern Matching and Logic
LispE, a modern Lisp dialect developed by Naver, introduces innovative constructs—
defpat
,
defmacro
, and
defpred
—that set it apart from traditional Lisp implementations like Common Lisp, Scheme, and Clojure. While Lisp dialects share a heritage of flexibility and macro systems, LispE extends this with advanced pattern matching, enhanced macro capabilities, and logic programming elements. This blog entry examines these features, comparing them to their counterparts in other Lisps with specific examples to highlight LispE’s unique approach.
defpat
: Pattern Matching in Function Definitions
LispE’s
defpat
enables defining multiple functions under the same name, each triggered by a specific argument pattern. This offers a declarative way to handle polymorphism beyond type-based dispatching.
LispE Example 1 (FizzBuzz):
(
defun
checkmod
(v d) (
eq
(% v d)
0
))
(defpat fizzbuzz ([integer_ (checkmod x
15
)])
'
fizzbuzz)
(defpat fizzbuzz ([integer_ (checkmod x
3
)])
'
fizz)
(defpat fizzbuzz ([integer_ (checkmod x
5
)])
'
buzz)
(defpat fizzbuzz (x) x)
(
mapcar
'
fizzbuzz (range
1
15
1
))
Output:
(1 2 fizz 4 buzz fizz 7 8 fizz buzz 11 fizz 13 14 fizzbuzz)
. The nested patterns (e.g.,
(integer_ (checkmod x 3))
) match integers divisible by 3, with a fallback for unmatched cases.
LispE Example 2 (Kleene Operator):
To further illustrate
defpat
’s capabilities, consider its support for Kleene operators (
+
,
*
,
%
), which allow matching sequences of arguments.
a% : means that the element is optional
a* : means that this element can be present 0 or n times
a+ : means that this element should be present at least once
Here’s an example that processes a list of numbers, collecting those less than 10:
(defpat collect-small ([(
<
x
10
)+ $ rest])
(println
"
Collected:
"
x
"
Remaining:
"
rest
)
x
)
(defpat collect-small (lst)
(println
"
No small numbers in:
"
lst)
'
()
)
(collect-small
'
(
5
8
12
3
15
))
Output:
Collected: (5 8) Remaining: (12 3 15)
(5 8)
Here,
[(< x 10)+ $ rest]
uses the
+
operator to match one or more numbers less than 10, binding them to
x
, while
$ rest
captures the remaining elements. If no numbers match the condition, the fallback definition applies. This demonstrates how
defpat
can concisely handle sequence patterns directly in the parameter list.

data.title: The Mutable OS: Why Isn't Windows Immutable in 2025?
data.author: ndegruchy
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了将Windows操作系统变为不可变系统的可能性和优势。不可变系统意味着操作系统是只读的，无法随意更改，确保系统稳定性。这种设计类似于早期的DeepFreeze软件，但更进一步。不可变系统通过整体替换系统镜像来更新，避免了部分更新失败或不兼容的问题。如果更新失败，系统会自动回滚到上一个正常状态。这种方法已经在macOS等系统中应用，降低了安全风险，并确保系统启动时的完整性。对于Windows来说，实现这种机制需要解决向后兼容性和配置管理的问题，但已有虚拟化和容器技术作为基础。这种设计不仅适用于操作系统，还可以应用于应用程序，确保其安装和运行的稳定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统中的不可变性和安全性机制

不同观点：
• [cedws] 认为Windows通过UFW（统一写入过滤器）实现了某种程度的不可变性。他提到可以通过基于RAM或磁盘的覆盖层来处理C盘分区，所有写入操作都会在该覆盖层中进行，并且可以被清除。不过，必须排除某些特定的路径，否则系统会出现问题。此外，覆盖层需要在sysprep阶段之后设置。

• [emchammer] 认为一个操作系统应该是自我托管的，即应该能够在同一台机器上编译和重新安装操作系统。他指出Windows和macOS由于是闭源的，无法实现这一点，并表示如果可以的话，他会选择这样做。

• [ndegruchy] 作为桌面技术支持人员，认为尽管操作系统安全性已经取得了很大进展，但不可变性仍然被视为一种异类。他对此感到不解，并希望听取其他人对这一问题的看法和反面观点。

• [mystified5016] 认为第三方供应商通过Windows更新向用户推送不需要的软件是导致问题的原因之一。他提到Windows会无故安装一些软件，比如他多次卸载的“Dell delivery service”或者某些打印机驱动程序。

• [fsflover] 认为如果关注安全性，应该考虑Qubes OS，这是一个通过硬件隔离实现安全性的操作系统。他表示这是他的日常驱动系统，并强烈推荐。

补充讨论：
• 关于Windows的不可变性实现存在技术细节的讨论，如覆盖层的设置和排除特定路径的问题。
• 对闭源操作系统（如Windows和macOS）在自我托管和安全性方面的局限性提出批评。
• 提到第三方软件和驱动程序在Windows操作系统中的不受欢迎安装现象。
• 推荐Qubes OS作为一种通过硬件隔离实现安全性和不可变性的替代方案。

43633195.article_content:
Today, I’d like to talk about Windows.
Wait, before you go, just hear me out: “What if Windows was an immutable OS?”
This idea might seem familiar to you. We actually had this, for some values of
’this’, back in the aughts. We called it
DeepFreeze
. Of course, it was more
about freezing the whole partition, and less of making the OS itself immutable,
but it was on the right path. Oh, but I haven’t explained “Immutable”.
What?
Immutable, at least as far as software goes, means to be unchanging. If you have
an immutable OS, then the OS is essentially read-only. You can’t make changes,
you can’t fiddle with it, and that’s by design. This doesn’t mean you
can’t
fiddle with it. Projects like Fedora Silverblue and NixOS allow you to fiddle
with the OS, just outside of the running context. Changes come in signed and
sealed updates to the
whole
system, not one-off patches. That means when you
boot your computer, the OS either works, or it doesn’t. If it doesn’t, then most
of these systems will roll back to the last working copy, with no leftover bits
or half-upgraded components. That means you have a solid foundation upon which
to work on.
In short: The system image is a fixed unit. It is what it is at install/update
time. When it comes time to patch, you just replace it, wholesale. If that fails
for whatever reason, the change doesn’t take place and you’re back to where you
were: Working.
We even do this already in the wild with applications. Flatpak, while I disagree
with it being a replacement for good package management, does this for applications.
Microsoft has it’s MSIX apps from the Windows Store and Apple’s built-in apps are
all contained on special partitions that get updated wholesale.
A Brief History
Culture around Operating Systems has evolved over the ~60 years of computing. In
the early days, MS-DOS was just some files on the disk that if you deleted or
modified would kill your system and require an expensive call to a tech. Later,
we organized those files and told people to stay out, but this was mostly
convention and not a hard and fast rule. OSes of the Unix variety did have
permissions to stop tampering, but these were pretty rudimentary and easy to
mess up.
As OSes have matured as the state of the industry has seen more harmful actors
willing data destruction or theft on users and organizations, we’ve put up more
roadblocks. Windows has mostly kept apace with this by erecting stronger
permission models and adding things like UAC and sandboxing with MSIX. Not all
of this is well received, but it’s the state of the system. However, a lot of
the problems that I, as a desktop support tech, see could probably be mitigated
by making the OS layer read-only.
Why?
When your OS is read-only. You, nor Bob, or Sally or xXx420BlazeItBigBallsxXx
can make changes to the system. That’s it. No more weird OS errors, trojans,
unbootable systems, half installed patches or corrupt system files. Your
computer turns on, and verifies the system is the way it’s supposed to be and
you go on your merry way. This allows folks like me and my security “friends” to
worry about your
data
more, and less about tweaking knobs so that you can’t
install 30 toolbars, delete
system32.dll
or get some drive-by-malware
infection from a advertisement.
The patching story cannot be undersold. When “Patch Tuesday” rolls around, you
don’t have to worry about it not finishing and leaving you in a half-working
state, or not applying
some
of the patches because of an improper order or
some weird lock on a file not being removed. The whole thing is replaced. If
that replacement doesn’t work, then you just reboot (probably being done anyway)
and you’re back to the last known good state.
This is being done already on macOS and lowers the effective surface area for
attacks to take root, and makes sure when you turn on your computer, it actually
turns on and boots up. The same system can also be used to ensure that applications
follow the same behavior. Installing Microsoft Office like this would ensure that
when you open Word, Word is what you get. Just like the OS, no more half-installed
configurations, broken components and reinstall/repair cycles to fix that toolbar
button.
How?
Well, that’s the billion-dollar question. There is some groundwork done for this
already. There is virtualization and container support in Windows and we already
have a lot of prior art in Faronics’ DeepFreeze software. The big missing area,
at least as I can see it is backwards-compatibility and handling overrides or
configurations.
The story doesn’t end with monoliths like Microsoft, Apple or Red Hat handing
off blessed OS images and you’re just forced to accept it. You can configure
things, make changes, and deploy images that are blessed. This even allows you
to layer configurations atop a blessed image to further customize it. Keeping
the OS layer pristine, the configurations in their own space and the user system
all separate, but perceptually unified components tha

data.title: Baking the Y Combinator from Scratch
data.author: mprast
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Y组合子（Y Combinator），一个在函数式编程中用于实现递归的数学构造。作者强调不仅要理解“是什么”，还要理解“如何实现”和“为什么重要”。Y组合子用于在不允许显式自引用的函数式语言中实现递归。其定义为：

$$ Y = \lambda f. \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) $$

文章分为两部分，第一部分解释Y组合子的构造及其如何产生固定点（fixed point），第二部分讨论其在递归中的应用。Y组合子由逻辑学家Haskell Curry提出，也被称为“固定点组合子”（Fixpoint Combinator）或“悖论组合子”（Paradoxical Combinator）。

Lambda演算中的一切都是函数，没有函数名，所有函数都是匿名函数。固定点是指对函数$f$，存在一个点$x$使得$f(x) = x$。Y组合子是一个固定点组合子，它接受一个单参数函数并返回该函数的一个固定点，满足$Y(f) = f(Y(f))$。

简言之，Y组合子通过实现固定点来支持递归，是函数式编程中一个重要工具。
