The
platform engineering toolkit
for Kubernetes
Koreo is a new approach to
Kubernetes configuration management and resource orchestration
empowering developers through programmable workflows and structured data
Get Started
Learn More
Programmable workflows
Define complex, multi-step processes that react to events and manage the lifecycle of your Kubernetes resources. Koreo workflows enable automation of everything from simple deployments to entire cloud environments. It's like programmingâor
choreographing
âKubernetes controllers.
Structured configuration management
Manage Kubernetes configurations the way they were intendedâas structured data, not just templated strings. This allows you to easily validate, transform, and combine configurations from multiple sources in a manageable and scalable way.
Dynamic resource materialization
Inject values from a config file or overlay partial definitions to build up a complete resource view. Combine configurations from different sources like security, compliance, and SRE, and even apply custom logic, to give developers a golden path for provisioning applications, resources, or anything Kubernetes manages.
Configuration as functions
Inspired by functional programming principles, Koreo lets you decompose configuration into functions. These functions act as reusable building blocks to encapsulate common tasks and logic within your Koreo workflows. This promotes modularity, reduces duplication, and makes workflows easier to maintain and evolve.
Declarative operator model
Define your desired state through workflows and functions, and Koreo will automatically reconcile the actual state to match. This declarative approach simplifies management and ensures consistency across your infrastructure.
First-class testing and tooling
Actually
treat configuration as code with Koreo's built-in testing framework and developer tooling. Write unit tests for individual functions and entire workflows to catch errors early and prevent unexpected behavior. Koreo's IDE integration gives you real-time feedback, autocomplete, and introspection.
Powerful configuration management
with flexible resource orchestration
Koreo is a platform engineering toolkit that introduces a new approach to configuration management and resource orchestration in Kubernetes. It builds upon the best aspects of tools like Helm, Kustomize, Argo, and Crossplane while addressing some of their limitations.
It serves as a meta-controller programming language and runtime
that allows you to compose off-the-shelf operators into cohesive platforms by orchestrating Kubernetes controllers. Through powerful primitives, Koreo enables DevOps and platform engineers to create dynamic workflows that automate everything from simple deployments to entire internal developer platforms. Its layered configuration management enables teams like security, compliance, or SRE to enforce consistent standards and practices for resources within your organization.
Workflows and functions
provide composable primitives for building platforms
Koreo empowers you to build complex Kubernetes platforms using composable workflows and functions
, drawing inspiration from functional programming principles. Workflows act as blueprints for platform operations, defining the steps for tasks like application deployments or infrastructure provisioning. Functions are the individual building blocks within these workflows, encapsulating specific logic for data transformation, API interaction, or resource creation. And with built-in testing, you can validate configuration and catch errors early in the development process.
The true power of Koreo lies in its ability to program these workflows. Incorporate conditional logic, loops, and error handling to create dynamic platform operations. Automate complex processes, enforce policies, and build self-service platforms for your development teams.

data.title: Why Tap a Wheel of Cheese?
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了帕尔马干酪（Parmigiano Reggiano）质量检测的独特过程，由一支24人的专业团队"battitori"负责。他们使用小金属锤敲击奶酪轮，通过声音在6-7秒内判断是否存在缺陷。文章跟随了两位battitori——37岁的Alessandro Stocchi和他81岁的导师Renato Giudici，展示了这一传统技艺的传承。检测时，奶酪轮被置于凳子上以避免杂音，通过敲击声判断内部结构是否 compact。奶酪被分为三个等级：最高质量适合长期陈化、次级质量建议尽早食用、有明显缺陷的作为普通餐桌奶酪。尽管有些缺陷是自然的产物，但整体瑕疵率很低。这一工作需要极大的热情和谦逊，且技艺通过实践代代相传。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意大利传统手工制作奶酪的过程及其与现代技术的平衡

不同观点：
• SamBam认为，尽管技术上可以实现奶酪检测的自动化，但保留传统手工制作方式有助于维持产品的高质量，避免工业化生产导致品质下降。传统不仅关乎生产本身，还关乎文化与情感。
• nancyminusone指出，在奶酪制作过程中已经部分使用了现代技术，例如电动搅拌机和机器人翻转奶酪轮。但他也提出疑问，在技术与传统之间应如何划清界限，是完全手工还是完全自动化。
• ziofill从个人体验出发，强调了Parmigiano Reggiano和Grana Padano作为意大利传统美食的独特美味，并分享了这些奶酪的多种食用方式，尤其是带皮使用。
• saltcured提到了一个关于人工检测的趣闻：在试图用机器模仿人工敲击检测时，发现人类专家实际上依赖的是气味而非声音，暗示人工检测的某些方面难以被技术完全取代。
• talkingtab鼓励自制奶酪，分享了一些YouTube视频资源，并以个人经验说明自制奶酪虽然困难但非常值得，强调了手工制作的乐趣。
• dfxm12对Parmigiano Reggiano缺乏品牌标识表示疑惑，并询问是否有人会选择特定产地的奶酪，反映出消费者对产品来源的关注。
• kazinator将奶酪手工检测比作汽车制造中的表面检查，认为这可能只是为了展示和娱乐观众，而实际质量检测应在后台进行。
• verelo分享了一个温馨的故事，讲述了从邻居老太太那里学到的意大利谚语“piano piano”（慢慢来），与手工制作奶酪的耐心与细致相呼应。
• taxicabjesus讲述了自己因食用工业奶酪导致健康问题，因此对意大利传统奶酪坚持使用天然成分表示赞赏，强调了工业食品中潜在的健康风险。
• 0xdeadbeefbabe对奶酪制作被视为专家的领域表示怀疑，认为可能存在过度商业化的问题，并质疑是否真的只有专家才能制作优质奶酪。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到手工制作与工业化生产的对立，部分评论者对手工制作的情感价值和文化意义表示支持，而另一些人则关注技术在提高生产效率方面的潜力。
• 争议的焦点之一是手工与自动化之间的平衡，尤其是在保证产品质量和传统的前提下如何合理使用技术。
• 消费者对食品来源和生产过程的关注也是一个重要话题，尤其是对品牌标识和传统制作方法的重视。

43644970.article_content:
Why Tap a Wheel of Cheese?
Renato Giudici demonstrates his skill photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
Behind the approximately 4 million wheels of Parmigiano Reggiano produced annually, there is a tiny team of 24 battitori responsible for ensuring the quality of each one. Armed with a small metal hammer, these specialized “drummers” tap every wheel after the minimum aging period of 12 months, and within 6-7 seconds they can detect if there are any defects, based purely on the sounds they hear.
Shadowing the Battitori
Author Kristine Jannuzzi with Alessandro Stocchi and Renato Giudici
I had the privilege of spending the morning with two of these maestros on the job in Emilia-Romagna: Alessandro Stocchi, a dynamic 37-year-old native of Reggio Emilia who began training to become a battitore in 2014, and his mentor, Renato Giudici, who at 81 years old, embodies a lifetime of passion for Parmigiano Reggiano. Renato is a former cheesemaker who made Parmigiano Reggiano for many years, and rather than retire, he chose to become a guardian of the King of Cheeses as a
battitore.
There’s no course to learn the niche skills and nuances of this trade; Alessandro accompanied and apprenticed with Renato and other experts for about 3 years, learning through firsthand experience how to assess each wheel.
“The particularity of this profession to me is that it’s like it was 200 years ago, and it’s a skill that’s handed down from generation to generation. You go around with the most expert, most experienced battitori, and you watch and listen to them, and slowly they start to give you the hammer. You try with them next to you, piano piano, and gradually, you begin to do more on your own,” explained Stocchi. “It’s a big responsibility, you have to be really capable of doing it, you can’t damage the cheese.”
How Parmigiano Reggiano is Evaluated
Alessandro Stocchi explains the grading system photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
Renato showed me the ideal setup, with a wheel of Parmigiano Reggiano flat on a stool underneath the one that is being evaluated, so there is no extraneous noise. If the sound is homogeneous throughout the tapping, there are no defects.
“We hit all of the surfaces of the cheese, and from the sound of the hammer against the surface we can imagine in our mind an Xray of the wheel and how it is internally. For a perfect wheel with no defects, the paste is completely compact, no empty space. If there are structural defects, such as little fissures or cavities, we can hear that the sound of the hammer is different,” explained Stocchi.
Parmigiano Reggiano Categories
A cheese wheel with double parallel lines photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
 Top quality, suitable for longer aging
 Lower quality, best consumed young
 Significant defects, not labeled Parmigiano Reggiano
There are three different categories to which the wheels are assigned. The first is perfect, or with negligible defects, and these wheels receive the fire-branded Parmigiano Reggiano mark. The second category with minor defects is still marked Parmigiano Reggiano, but the rind is engraved with parallel lines to indicate to the consumer that this is not the highest level, and probably best consumed young. And the third category is for wheels with more significant flaws, and the rind and all identifying marks are removed, so the cheese is sold as generic table cheese.
Renato Giudici taps a wheel photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
“Sometimes when I do events and find a defect while I’m tapping a wheel, people who are watching turn their noses up. But to me it’s a beautiful thing that there are defects, and I’m not just saying it because if there aren’t any, I lose my job,” says Stocchi, laughing. “But the fact that there are defects indicates even more the artisanal quality of our product—we work with raw milk, without preservatives, each year there are many variations. Anyone who works with something in nature knows that not everything always goes how we would want or expect. I always say the day when we have 100% perfect Parmigiano Reggiano, we’d have to ask ourselves some questions, because it’s not an industrial product, so it’s normal that sometimes there are flaws.”
The number of wheels with defects remains low; in recent years, approximately 10% fell into the second category, and only about 1.5% were classified as third category.
“To do this job requires great passion, respect, and humility. My elder colleagues tell me you never stop learning, even after 50 years of doing it,” recounted Stocchi. “The day you think you’ve learned everything is the day you’ll start making errors.”
Cheese Education
Kristine Jannuzzi
April 8, 2025

data.title: Arroyo (YC W23) has been acquired by Cloudflare
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 2025年4月10日，Arroyo团队宣布已被Cloudflare收购，旨在将无服务器SQL流处理功能引入Cloudflare开发者平台，并与Queues、Workers和R2等服务集成。Arroyo引擎将继续保持开源，并支持自托管。此次收购由Arroyo首席执行官Micah Wylde宣布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare收购Arroyo及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **销售服务问题**：[prennert] 提到Cloudflare的销售服务不佳，尝试开设企业账户但未能联系到销售人员，质疑其客户支持能力，并询问是否有其他支持PHI数据传输的替代方案。
• **开放源码收购的信誉**：[esafak] 关注Cloudflare在维护开放源码收购方面的声誉，质疑其是否能有效管理这些项目。
• **营利公司收购开放源码的目的**：[mentalgear] 质疑营利公司收购开放源码项目的动机和可行性，提出这些项目是否真的能被“买断”的问题。
• **技术对比**：[rebanevapustus] 对Arroyo与类似技术（如Materialize或Feldera）进行比较，认为Arroyo可能功能较少，提出其独特价值的问题。

补充讨论：
• **祝贺与个人支持**：[jeffchao]、[Hansenq]、[brandonb] 等人对收购表示祝贺，[jeffchao] 特别提到对Arroyo在Cloudflare中如何整合和提升流媒体功能的兴趣。
• **功能优先级**：[moonikakiss] 关心Arroyo是否会优先集成Iceberg/R2目录的流媒体功能。
• **收购价格**：[ilrwbwrkhv] 对收购价格表示关注，直接询问收购金额。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare在客户支持和开放源码项目管理方面的能力和信誉存在质疑。
• Arroyo相对于其他类似技术的优势和独特性不明确，引发技术价值讨论。

这些观点反映了社区对Cloudflare收购Arroyo的多方面关注，包括客户体验、技术价值和公司战略等。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）的实际效能、应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **mrdependable** 认为当前的AI（如Claude）在解决实际问题时表现不如预期，尤其是在调试代码等实际任务中。他指出大型语言模型（LLM）存在一个问题，即使用者很难引导它们脱离某种输出模式，且AI在反向推理和问题定位上表现不佳。他还将此问题与Google搜索的局限性进行了类比。
  
• **simonw** 关注数据的可访问性和分析工具的应用。他将报告中的数据转换为SQLite数据库，并提供了探索数据的工具链接，展示了报告中关于模型偏见的有趣表格，侧重于数据分析和工具分享，而非直接评价AI性能。

data.title: We Designed TigerBeetle's Docs from Scratch
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: TigerBeetle团队从零开始重建了其文档网站，以符合TigerStyle和第一性原理的思维方式，而不仅限于数据库本身。他们最初使用Docusaurus来快速搭建文档原型，但发现它违背了团队的“零依赖”原则，引入了过多依赖和复杂性，且生成的额外文件影响了GitHub上的纯净展示，搜索功能也不理想。团队希望文档与数据库本身一样精益求精，因此决定创建一个简洁、清晰、快速的阅读体验。新的文档网站依赖Zig编译器，使用Pandoc进行Markdown解析，以确保内容在各种形式下的一致性，并通过Zig的构建系统实现增量更新。最终，文档网站不仅提升了外部用户体验，也优化了内部代码实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TigerBeetle团队从零开始构建文档网站的工程决策是否合理，及其相关技术选择的讨论。

不同观点：
• **mtlynch**：对该工程决策持怀疑态度。认为团队可能是为了趣味性而做了非最佳选择。他指出多个现有工具（如Hugo、Pelican、Eleventy）可以实现类似效果，且对文中提到的安全策略（CSP）持批评态度，认为防止XSS攻击的解释过于牵强，存在其他更简单的缓解风险方式。
  
• **bognition**：支持该决策，认为在当前依赖现成工具的时代，TigerBeetle团队选择自主构建文档网站是一种令人耳目一新的做法。文档是其产品的核心部分，因此自主构建可以更好地满足自身需求，且最终效果出色。

• **bryanhogan**：虽然认可自建文档网站的效果，但提出可以使用其他工具（如Starlight、Vitepress、Nextra）来达到类似目的，暗示这些工具可能是更优选择。

• **hakkotsu**：关注TigerBeetle网站主页上出现的人物（Primeagen）可能带来的品牌形象不匹配问题，担心一个以“混乱和争议”著称的人物与金融数据库所需的“绝对可靠性”不符。

• **systemswizard**：完全否定该决策，认为这仅仅是营销手段，不具备实际技术价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于TigerBeetle团队是否有必要从零开始构建文档网站，以及其安全策略（CSP）的合理性。
• mtlynch指出团队对CSP的使用存在误解，并提供了额外信息来澄清，但最终仍持怀疑态度。
• 其他评论者更多关注工具选择和品牌形象问题，而非具体技术细节。

43610566.article_content:
Why We Designed TigerBeetle's Docs from Scratch
Feb 27, 2025
Fabian RÃ¼hle
Fabio Arnold
matklad
We recently rebuilt TigerBeetleâs docs site from scratch. We wanted
to apply TigerStyle and first principles thinking, not only to our
database but also to our docs. To give users the fastest possible
experience, given how much time they spend reading, and to do this
without the dependency of Docusaurus. At TigerBeetle,
how
we
build things is as important as
what
we build, because
methodology has a second order effect on motivation.
In the Beginning there were Dinosaurs
When TigerBeetle was founded,
Docusaurus
was used to prototype our
docs site. It was quick to start, and we could maintain
our
docs in our main GitHub repository
.
There were, however, some downsides:
Violation of our zero dependency principle: as Docusaurus is based
on NodeJS, it added
a
lot of dependencies
to our code base. We have a check that no large
files are committed to git, and package-lock.json failed this
check.
Complexity: Docusaurus is fundamentally a complex piece of software
â a React app. While itâs good at what it does, we believe that an
equally good result can be achieved with simpler methods.
Unwanted additional code: Docusaurus adds
extra
artifacts
within the Markdown files which also show up visibly on
GitHub (i.e. metadata and extra
_category_.json
files) and
we wanted GitHubâs representation of our docs to be pure.
Sub-optimal search: the search experience provided through an
external service, was a bit fuzzy and not optimally integrated.
But, most importantly, we wanted to treat our documentation as a
part of the database itself. That means that docs must use the same
standard of craftsmanship we put into the database proper, or they wonât
feel
like an integral part of the database.
Docusaurus served well as a prototype but the time for change had
arrived. We set out to create the experience weâd prefer when browsing
and reading documentation: simple, clear, and fast. With not only a
great âexternalâ user experience but also a great âinternalâ user
experience (the implementation of the code itself, when you pop the
hood, e.g. the footprint over the network). So the path we took was
shaped not only by our design but also our engineering
considerations.
As Clean as a Book
How could we provide the best reading experience for our readers? The
reading experience should be as clean and simple as a book. We wanted to
remove as many distractions as possible, to keep the design
minimalistic. We gave the content more space by removing elements like
breadcrumbs, table of contents, footer and by integrating the top
navigation into the left side navigation. We switched dark/light mode
automatically based on your system settings, so you wouldnât have to
toggle that manually (and so we wouldnât bring in any chrome for that)
and made it possible to hide the side navigation or adjust its width for
maximum focus.
Website Ã  la carte
Given that TigerBeetleâs only dependency is the Zig compiler, we
started exploring what a static site generator (SSG) based on Zig could
look like. At the time, our friend
Loris
Cro
was building his own SSG,
Zine
, and
some companies
were already using it to generate their docs
.
We got excited and considered Zine. However, Zine uses SuperMD,
described as an extension to Markdown and fundamentally a different type
of Markdown. Itâs important to understand that our docs are content
first, and can be viewed in three different forms:
As raw text in your editor of choice
On GitHub
On our
website
For this reason, it is required that the content is GitHub-flavored
Markdown (
GFM
). And
unfortunately, we found some incompatibilities between SuperMD and GFM.
For example, by design, SuperMD does not support raw inline HTML while
GFM does. Instead of rewriting our docs using only the subset that is
supported by both GFM and SuperMD, we decided to explore more
optionsâ¦
To be honest, the hard part of static site generation is parsing the
Markdown, since Markdown is a complex language. Everything around it is
simple scripting, which we can easily do ourselves. Luckily, there is
Pandoc
â a rock solid tool created by the
editor of the CommonMark specification himself. So we made an exception
to depend on it. We use Zigâs built-in package manager to pull in Pandoc
as a single statically built executable (verifying its hash of course)
and then use Zigâs build system to parallelize the translation of
Markdown source files into the final HTML. (Fun fact: this blog is
generated using the same setup!)
You can find the full implementation
on
GitHub
, but, for the purposes of this blog post, weâll actually
write a tiny prototype right on the spot. This is a useful exercise, as
this tiny program teaches
a lot
about the philosophy behind
build.zig
!
The big picture is that we cast the entire static site generation as
just a build task for the Zig build system. This will get us incremental
updates fo

data.title: Blue Shield Data Breach (Google Ads)
data.author: bix6
data.article_summary: 2025年4月2日，300名加州蓝盾（Blue Shield of California）的志愿者齐聚一堂，通过参与社区服务活动纪念 César Chávez 和 Dolores Huerta 的贡献。志愿者们投入到各种公益项目中，如食品分发、社区花园建设和教育工作坊，以实际行动弘扬两人为劳工权利和公平正义所作的努力。这次活动不仅表达了对两位民权领袖的敬意，还促进了社区团结和服务精神。加州蓝盾表示，将继续支持此类公益活动，推动社会进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Blue Shield公司披露其用户数据被不当分享给Google广告产品的事件，以及对此事件的回应和用户反应。

不同观点：
• [bix6] 认为Blue Shield的行为令人失望。他引用了公司的声明，指出在2021年4月至2024年1月期间，Google Analytics的配置错误导致用户数据被分享给Google Ads，可能包括受保护的健康信息。尽管公司声称没有外部不良行为者参与，且Google未将信息用于其他目的或分享给第三方，但[bix6]对这种数据泄露事件表示不满。

• [olyjohn] 对事件表示极度愤怒和不信任。他质疑公司在披露该事件时还在要求用户提供更多信息，暗示这种做法非常不恰当。他的评论充满情绪化表达，反映出对数据隐私问题的强烈反感。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Blue Shield对用户数据的不当处理以及用户对隐私泄露的担忧。用户对公司保证"没有坏人参与"的说辞并不买账，显示出对数据安全的深刻不信任。
• [olyjohn] 的评论还暗示了对公司在处理用户数据时的时机的质疑，特别是在用户已经对隐私问题感到担忧的情况下，仍要求用户提供更多信息，进一步加剧了用户的不满。
• 数据隐私和安全问题成为讨论的核心，尤其是涉及敏感的健康信息时，用户的担忧和愤怒更为明显。

data.title: Show HN: Pledge – A Lightweight Reactive Framework for Swift (No Rx Overhead)
data.author: gokulnair2001
data.article_summary: Pledge是一个轻量级、线程安全的Swift反应式编程框架，简化了状态管理和事件传播。它提供了简洁灵活的方式来实现观察者模式，支持线程安全、优先级通知、自定义传递队列、批量更新、速率限制（节流和去抖动）以及函数式操作符等功能。核心组件包括`PLObservable`，用于创建可观察值，以及`PLGlobalStore`，用于集中管理全局状态。Pledge还支持控制通知传递的队列和优先级，并提供批量更新和速率限制功能，以优化性能和资源使用。安装通过Swift Package Manager完成，便于集成和使用。

Pledge
A thoughtfully designed reactive programming framework in Swift
Pledge is a lightweight, thread-safe reactive programming framework for Swift that simplifies state management, event propagation and balances power with simplicity in your applications. While other frameworks force you to learn complex concepts and operators, Pledge focuses on solving the real problems developers face daily:
Overview
Pledge provides a clean, flexible way to implement the observer pattern in Swift applications. It enables you to create observable values that notify subscribers of changes, with powerful features like:
Thread-safe implementation
Priority-based notifications
Customizable delivery queues
Batch updates
Rate limiting (throttling and debouncing)
Functional operators (map, filter, etc.)
Global state management

data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了市政消防车与机场消防车的主要区别。市政消防车主要应对城市、郊区和乡村的各种火灾和紧急情况，根据社区需求配备不同水箱和设备，需要在25秒内从0加速到35英里/小时，最高时速至少50英里。而机场救援与消防车辆（ARFF）则专门设计用于机场环境，处理飞机坠毁、燃油泄漏等紧急情况，要求在25秒内从0加速到50英里/小时，最高时速至少70英里。ARFF车辆通常携带更多水和专用灭火剂，以迅速应对涉及飞机的高风险事故。Oshkosh的Striker® 8x8是其中性能最佳的ARFF车辆之一。

Blog
The Difference Between Municipal Fire Trucks and Airport Fire Trucks
January 24, 2023
{count-facebook}
{count-twitter}
{count-linkedin}
{count-pinterest}
Firefighters respond to a wide range of emergencies across every type of environment and the equipment they use must be able to meet the demands of each situation.
Serving a vast array of communities, including urban, rural and airport settings, firefighters use different types of fire apparatus—all with unique configurations and attributes to complete the scenarios faced each day.
This blog walks through several key differences between municipal and airport fire trucks.
Types of Calls
The most obvious difference between municipal fire apparatus and aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles are the types of emergency calls that they respond to.
Municipal Fire Service Calls
Municipal fire trucks are the most recognizable emergency firefighting vehicles. The type of fire apparatus a department needs is determined by the mission of the truck and the community it serves each day.
Urban fire apparatus
: Fire departments in urban areas may respond to emergencies on city streets that are narrow and require apparatus with superior maneuverability to navigate tight turns and corners. Oftentimes, fire stations in urban areas are historic with confined spaces, requiring more compact apparatus that will fit in the building while still providing modern firefighting capabilities.
Suburban fire apparatus
: As growth occurs outside of cities with the expansion of commercial and residential communities, fire departments need to keep a pulse of the continual progression of land use and building types to match services and apparatus accordingly.
Rural fire apparatus
: Rural firefighters may respond to a large number of motor vehicle accidents, particularly on remote roads, requiring ample compartmentation for first-aid and extraction equipment. Rural fire apparatus generally require larger water tanks to meet limited water supply events and for allowing times for greater distance in response time to building fires from other departments. Additionally, rural apparatus may be called to grass or marsh fires which require off-road capabilities.
The ability to arrive at an emergency or fire scene quickly is a critical attribute of a municipal fire truck. The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) requires municipal fire trucks must be able to accelerate from 0 to 35 miles per hour in 25 seconds and reach a top speed of at least 50 miles per hour.
ARFF Service Calls
While both ARFF vehicles and municipal fire trucks are equipped with a variety of tools to help them respond to emergencies, ARFF vehicles have a specialized design and some unique attributes specific for use in an airport environment. ARFF vehicles respond to many types of calls, including airplane crash scenes, other airplane emergencies such as wheel or brake fires, medical or fire emergencies at the terminal, ground support for fuel spills, or off-airport response for events like car fires in the parking garage and foam for municipal calls.
ARFF crews are faced with harsh conditions and hazardous scenes, including exposure to toxic fumes and chemicals, explosion risks, debris and more. Adding to the complexity of these demands is the fact that most of the world’s airports have a vastly different footprint, yet responders are required to arrive at a scene, whether on or off road, in three minutes or less at any time of the day.
The NFPA sets a higher standard for acceleration for ARFF vehicles. This is due in part to the critical nature of reaching a scene before a fire gets to an aircraft’s tanks where extremely flammable jet fuel is stored. ARFF vehicles are required to have the capability to accelerate from 0 to 50 miles per hour in 25 seconds or less and reach a top speed of at least 70 miles per hour. Often, the ARFF vehicle’s response time is aided by the relatively short distances needed to travel in an enclosed airport environment.
Known as the most capable ARFF vehicle ever built and custom-engineered to deliver rapid response, Oshkosh Airport Products’
Striker® 8x8
reaches 50 mph (80 kph) in less than 20 seconds with fewer emissions while exceeding NFPA, ICAO and EU standards.
Water Supply
Water is the most common and recognizable method of suppressing fires. Both municipal and airport fire trucks use water to fight fires, but the trucks are often equipped with vastly different amounts of water.
Municipal Fire Truck Water Supply
Fire departments strategically design fleet vehicles to match the needs of a community. As such, you may find some apparatus with ample water supply and some with none at all. It often depends on water infrastructure and fleet management.
Typically, municipal fire trucks have one of the following water tank sizes:
500-gallon
750-gallon
1000-gallon

data.title: AmigaOS Updated in 2025
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 2025年，比利时软件公司Hyperion Entertainment发布了AmigaOS 3.2的第三次更新（版本3.2.3），特别针对配备680x0处理器及PiStorm加速板的Amiga电脑。此次更新提升了色彩表现和分辨率。尽管更新时间不规律，但Hyperion对操作系统的持续投入值得肯定，尤其是公司在经历股东破产和所有权变更后依然坚持开发。此外，AmigaOS 4继续支持PowerPC处理器的Amiga设备，而第三方操作系统MorphOS也仍在更新。与此同时，AROS研发操作系统正开发Arm移植版本，目前在x86 PC上表现最佳。总体而言，Amiga社区在硬件选择上偏向PowerPC的决策受到质疑，但复古计算爱好者仍有许多选择。

OSes

AmigaOS updated in 2025 for some reason
9
Hyperion ships another patch, which is nice
Liam Proven
Thu 10 Apr 2025
//
14:53 UTC
Belgian software house Hyperion Entertainment has released
Update 3
for AmigaOS
3.2
, the version of the classic operating system it launched in 2021. The update targets Amigas with 680x0 processors, including systems enhanced with
PiStorm accelerator boards
.
AmigaOS 3.2.3 is more colorful and much higher-resolution than it has been
The schedule is irregular, but you can't fault Hyperion's commitment to updating its version of the OS, given that the previous release, AmigaOS 3.1, was in 1991. It brought version 3.1
back to life in 2016
, and that was followed by version 3.2 in May 2021. Since then, the company published
version 3.2.1
in December 2021, and then
version 3.2.2
in March 2023, as we
covered at the time
.
The release is also good news especially given more troubling developments at Hyperion. The company's largest shareholder, Ben Hermans BV,
went bankrupt
, after which the company
announced new ownership
(the "CVBA" on the end of its name stands for Coöperatieve Vennootschap Met Beperkte Aansprakelijkheid, a
limited liability cooperative
).
Haage & Partner's AmigaOS 3.9 running inside Amiga Forever – a little more colorful than in the old days
We reported on the
sale of the AmigaOS source code
way back in 2004. That led to Hyperion's other OS product,
AmigaOS 4
, which targets Amigas with PowerPC processors, such as the
Amiga X1000 that
The Reg
covered in 2010
, or the
X5000
. Both are from
A-EON Technology
, and as head honcho Trevor Dickinson's
latest blog post
puts it: "For us Amiga enthusiasts, 2025 is a milestone year — the 40th anniversary of the Amiga's creation."
PiStorm turbocharges vintage Amigas with the Raspberry Pi
AmigaOS 3.2.2 released for those feeling nostalgic
Amiga Fast File System makes minor comeback in new Linux kernel
New Amiga to go on sale in late 2017
A-EON's machines aren't the only PowerPC-based Amiga-compatibles. There were also the
Pegasos
,
Pegasos II
and
Efika 5200B
from Genesi, which ran a third-party AmigaOS-compatible OS called
MorphOS
. MorphOS is still around, and its latest version,
3.19
, came out in January. As well as Genesi kit,
MorphOS also supports
the AmigaOne 500 and Amiga X5000, plus several models of G4 and G5 Apple PowerMac (
The Reg
FOSS desk has an older version on a Mac mini G4).
AROS 1.2 for 68K, also in Amiga Forever. Not identical, but certainly very familiar
From the perspective of 2025, it looks like the Amiga world backed the wrong RISC-y horse with PowerPC. In hindsight, we wish they'd opted for Arm hardware instead. A Raspberry Pi 400 running an Arm-native Amiga-compatible OS would be great fun. For now, the next best thing for mass-market hardware is the
AROS Research Operating System
. This mainly targets x86 PC compatibles, although there's also a version for classic Amiga kit. There is a work-in-progress
Arm port
, but the current version works best hosted under Arm Linux. ®

43646362.article_summary: 2025年，比利时软件公司Hyperion Entertainment发布了AmigaOS 3.2的第三次更新（版本3.2.3），特别针对配备680x0处理器及PiStorm加速板的Amiga电脑。此次更新提升了色彩表现和分辨率。尽管更新时间不规律，但Hyperion对操作系统的持续投入值得肯定，尤其是公司在经历股东破产和所有权变更后依然坚持开发。此外，AmigaOS 4继续支持PowerPC处理器的Amiga设备，而第三方操作系统MorphOS也仍在更新。与此同时，AROS研发操作系统正开发Arm移植版本，目前在x86 PC上表现最佳。总体而言，Amiga社区在硬件选择上偏向PowerPC的决策受到质疑，但复古计算爱好者仍有许多选择。

data.title: How University Students Use Claude
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学生使用AI（尤其是LLM如ChatGPT和Claude）在学业中的影响，包括作弊问题、学习过程的改变以及对教育的长期影响。

不同观点：
• **AI作弊问题广泛存在**：dtnewman认为，学生广泛使用AI来作弊，例如直接将作业粘贴到ChatGPT中获取答案，这削弱了学习过程。他指出，AI让学习变得过于容易，使得学生错过了通过挣扎和思考来真正掌握知识的机会。

• **AI对学习的深层次影响**：defgeneric强调，AI不仅会导致作弊问题，还可能破坏深度学习过程。他指出，学术学习需要通过挣扎和思考来内化知识，而AI的即时答案会阻碍这一过程，最终可能导致学生无法真正掌握知识。

• **AI公司有动机淡化作弊问题**：SamBam认为，Anthropic等AI公司有动机淡化学生使用AI写论文等作弊行为，因为他们可能会刻意模糊或掩盖这些问题的严重性。

• **AI使用数据需要更透明**：walleeee指出，虽然文章试图正面描述AI的使用，但数据表明许多学生使用AI直接获取答案，而非进行深度学习。这表明AI可能成为分化技术，而非普及教育的工具。

• **技术细节学习的重要性**：sebstefan对技术解释和解决方案被混在一起报告表示不满，认为理解底层技术细节对于学习至关重要。

• **AI对写作和思维的影响**：dagw和zebomon讨论了AI对写作和思维的影响。他们认为，写作是思维的体现，过度依赖AI写作可能导致学生失去思考和表达的能力。

• **如何避免AI对学习的负面影响**：moojacob作为学生，提出了如何避免在使用AI时阻碍学习的担忧，并分享了个人经验。他担心使用AI会让他错过通过犯错学习的宝贵机会。

• **AI作为学习工具的潜力**：pugio分享了积极使用AI进行自学的经验，认为AI可以作为强大的学习辅助工具，帮助学生更高效地掌握知识。

• **重新定义作弊和教育的意义**：_tom_提出，作弊的定义需要根据AI时代的现实进行调整。他认为，教育应该为学生准备面对一个充满AI的职业生涯，而不是坚持过时的教学方法。

• **多数学生使用AI避免学习**：karpour认为，尽管AI工具能够帮助学习，但大多数学生实际上用它来避免学习。

• **不同教育阶段和LLM提供商的影响差异**：bluehatbrit对不同LLM提供商和教育阶段的使用情况表示好奇，并分享了其妻子在英国中学教学中观察到的学生使用Snapchat LLM的案例。

补充讨论：
• **AI对未来职业的影响**：_tom_的观点引发了关于AI对未来职业和教育目标的影响的讨论，强调教育需要适应AI时代的变化。

• **AI在学习中的潜在正面作用**：ozarkerD分享了个人经历，认为AI可以激发好奇心，成为学生探索知识的强大工具。

争议焦点：
• **AI在教育中的角色**：一方认为AI是作弊工具，严重破坏学习过程；另一方则认为AI是强大的学习辅助工具，可以帮助学生更高效地学习。
• **作弊定义的改变**：是否应根据AI的普及重新定义作弊和教育的意义，以适应未来的职业需求。

data.title: How much do you think it costs to make a pair of Nike shoes in Asia?
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 文章提到在x.com网站上，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会导致问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，可以尝试再次操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：全球供应链与制造业成本分析，特别是中美之间的经济竞争与鞋类产品的生产和定价问题。

不同观点：
• **Rayiner**：认为美国需要正视中国在科技领域的崛起，尤其是在核能、AI、电动车和电池等领域。他预测中国在经济总量上将超过美国，并质疑美国未来的竞争优势。他担心美国可能会像如今的英国一样，在全球产业链中失去实际生产优势，仅保留金融和服务业的优势。

• **hx8**：质疑鞋类产品定价中的利润分配问题。他质疑为什么Footlocker在成本上升时需要提高利润，而不是保持固定的利润率，尤其是当运营成本（如广告和零售空间）是固定时。

• **TrapLord_Rhodo**：批评文章使用假设的鞋款价格作为依据，指出高端品牌鞋即使在中国制造，也能卖出高价，强调品牌效应在定价中的作用。

• **aimor**：试图通过具体数字分析鞋类产品在不同环节中的成本分配，特别是在加征关税后的成本变化，并提出美国制造商如何在成本上与进口产品竞争的问题。

• **ZeroGravitas**：引用喜剧歌曲讽刺低成本制造背后的道德问题，特别是使用廉价劳动力的现象，质疑为何消费者仍需支付较高价格。

• **phkahler**：对供应链中各环节的百分比加价模式提出疑问，不理解为何每个环节都需要按成本百分比加价，而不是固定利润。

• **hnburnsy**：指出文章中对Footlocker的折扣计算存在模糊，认为实际销售价格和财务报告中的数字不一致，并讨论零售商和品牌自营店的不同成本结构。

• **ctrlp**：从消费者角度出发，关注鞋子的耐用性和长期使用成本，而不是仅仅看购买价格，质疑低价鞋的质量和使用寿命。

• **raincom**：分享在零售业工作的负面经验，质疑美国应创造什么样的工作岗位，是低质量的零售工作还是制造业工作。

• **jimt1234**：对特定类型鞋子（如Crocs）的制造成本提出疑问，认为其成本应非常低，因其生产工艺简单。

• **subsubzero**：通过历史价格对比，指出Nike通过外包和供应链效率降低产品价格，同时分析赞助和市场营销对最终售价的影响，建议通过提高售价或减少赞助费来促进美国制造业回流。

• **ZiiS**：认为文章使用了一些夸张手法，指出Nike等品牌的大部分利润用于广告和赞助，并认为市场需求会决定生产技术和成本的变化。

• **ForOldHack**：质疑文章中关于亚洲工人待遇的统计数据，基于自身经历指出实际工资水平远低于报道，并认为文章缺乏对现实的准确反映。

• **ungreased0675**：指出实际市场中亚洲制造的鞋子售价接近美国制造的鞋子，强调产品在价值链中的巨大加价现象。

补充讨论：
- 文章和评论中多次提到品牌效应、市场营销和赞助费用对最终产品价格的影响，特别是在高端鞋类市场中。
- 多个评论关注美国和中国在制造业和科技领域的竞争，以及未来全球经济格局的变化。
- 对供应链各环节的成本分配和利润加成模式存在较大争议，特别是各环节的定价逻辑和实际成本结构。

data.title: Tech CEO: 4-day work week didn't hurt or help productivity
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: Civo的CEO马克·博斯特（Mark Boost）接受采访时表示，公司自2021年起实施四天工作制，虽然生产力没有明显提升或下降，但员工反馈积极，有助于吸引和留住人才。员工大多选择周五休息，获得三天的周末，以便处理个人事务。然而，销售和客服等部门因需要五日覆盖，面临一定挑战，通过增加人手解决。尽管微软和戴尔曾试验四天工作制并取得积极成果，但未广泛推行。总体来看，四天工作制在科技行业中仍存在实施难度，但员工满意度显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：四天工作制与五天工作制的效率对比

不同观点：
• 观点一：四天工作制显示了五天工作制中存在大量冗余时间。如果四天工作制能够维持同样的产出，意味着在五天工作制中，员工并没有充分利用所有的工作时间。这暗示了员工在当前的工作周中可能存在低效或时间浪费的情况。（支持方：mytailorisrich）
    └─ 论据或例子：通过转向四天工作制可以揭示五天工作制中的低效率问题。

• 观点二：四天工作制可能提高了工作效率。因为员工在更短的工作周内必须更加专注和高效，以完成相同的工作量，这可能促使人们减少拖延和分心。（隐含观点：四天工作制可以激励更高的生产力）
    └─ 论据或例子：较短的工作周可能迫使员工优化时间管理，从而提升整体效率。

• 观点三：工作产出不能单纯通过工作天数来衡量。有些人认为工作的质量和产出与工作时间长短并非线性相关，而与员工的工作状态、任务复杂性等因素有关。因此，转向四天工作制不一定会减少产出，反而可能增加员工的幸福感和工作满意度。（支持方：可能反对单纯关注时间长短的人）
    └─ 论据或例子：四天工作制可能提高员工幸福感，从而间接提高工作效率和质量。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：四天工作制是否真的能保持与五天工作制相同的工作产出，以及是否存在冗余时间是讨论的核心。一部分人认为它揭示了五天工作制的低效，而另一部分人则认为四天工作制能激励更高的效率和工作满意度。
  
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：评论中隐含了对工作效率和员工幸福感之间关系的思考，四天工作制可能不仅仅是减少工作时间，还涉及整体工作生活质量的提升。

43644572.article_content:
Offbeat
6
Tech CEO: 4-day work week didn't hurt or help productivity
6
'There are challenges' but staff recruitment and retention isn't one of them
Paul Kunert
Thu 10 Apr 2025
//
11:57 UTC
Interview
Civo shifted its workforce to a four-day working week and while it hasn't changed productivity much at the cloud biz, it has helped attract "new talent" and retain existing staff, CEO Mark Boost says.
While Microsoft and Dell would prefer to keep quiet about work-life balance programs embarked upon during 2019 and 2022 respectively, others in the tech industry – albeit of a different scale – are embracing change.
"We piloted the four-day week in 2020 and after a successful pilot, which included gathering feedback from our staff, we decided to implement it in January 2021, so we're now four years on from adopting full time," he tells
The Register
.
"During our original pilot we saw no decline in productivity (I wouldn't say we had any gain). However, the feedback was super positive and staff liked the extra day off and felt they had a much better work-life balance.
"Every employee is on a four-day week and most employees opted for Fridays off, which gives them a three-day weekend and I know many employees have said it allows them an opportunity on a Friday to catch-up on personal tasks/admin, allowing them more freedom on Saturday/Sunday."
Brit consultancy 4 Day Week Foundation last month launched a campaign to get more local
tech businesses to adopt new working styles
. It is starting trials for the latest batch of entrants from the end of June.
Is this out of sync with an industry better known for pushing people hard to work long hours? Google co-founder Sergey Brin recently said he wanted AI engineers in the office at least five days a week,
working 60-plus hour weeks
.
"It's also been great for us to attract new talent and has helped us retain talent. We didn't need a restructure at all, but in certain roles we need coverage on Fridays and often weekends too (e.g. customer support), so we have to flex time and ensure we have enough rotation to ensure we have enough coverage," says Boost.
Everyone at Civo does their full week's hours during the four days. While it may be good for the staff, is it a headache for management?
"The four-day week does present some challenges across certain departments, e.g. sales and customer support where we need coverage beyond four days, but we've been able to work around this by hiring extra people to improve our coverage."
91% of polled Amazon staff unhappy with return-to-office, 3-in-4 want to jump ship
Results are in for biggest 4-day work week trial ever: 92% sticking with it
Next six months could set a new pace for work-life balance
Most Londoners would quit before they give up working from home
Despite its reluctance to talk to
The Reg
about why it hasn't expanded its own initiative, Microsoft said in 2019 that its trial of a four-day week in Japan made for happier staff, more efficient meetings, and a 40 percent increased productivity rate.
"Work a short time, rest well, and learn a lot,"
Microsoft Japan president and CEO Takuya Hirano said
at the time. "I want employees to think about and experience how they can achieve the same results with 20 percent less working time."
The added bonus was also lower operating costs in terms of electricity and printed pages. In these times of Microsoft spending big on AI datacenters, eking out efficiencies make more sense. We previously asked Microsoft why it hasn't rolled out the scheme to more offices across the world.
A spokesperson told us they'd look into our inquiry and "let you know if we have anything to add." Since then? Crickets.
Dell is the same. Staff seemingly loved the four-day week but it didn't expand beyond
tests in the Netherlands and Argentina
. Dell didn't respond to requests for comment.
Maybe it's investor anxiety. Or maybe tech's billionaire class still prefers the go-hard-or-go-home ethos. ®

    └─ 论据或例子：较短的工作周可能迫使员工优化时间管理，从而提升整体效率。

    └─ 论据或例子：四天工作制可能提高员工幸福感，从而间接提高工作效率和质量。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：评论中隐含了对工作效率和员工幸福感之间关系的思考，四天工作制可能不仅仅是减少工作时间，还涉及整体工作生活质量的提升。

data.title: The Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 谷歌云推出了一种名为Agent2Agent（A2A）的新开放协议，旨在实现AI代理之间的互操作性。该协议允许不同厂商或框架开发的代理安全地交换信息并协同工作，从而提升自动化水平和生产力，降低长期成本。A2A获得了Atlassian、Salesforce、SAP等50多家技术伙伴以及Accenture、Deloitte等服务供应商的支持。该协议基于现有标准如HTTP、SSE和JSON-RPC，支持多种模式和长时间任务，确保企业能够在不同平台和云环境中管理代理。A2A通过“代理卡”实现能力发现，并通过客户端和远程代理的交互完成任务管理，推动企业工作流的自动化和创新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A2A和MCP协议的目的、区别及其实际应用价值

不同观点：
• zellyn和Flux159关注A2A和MCP协议的技术细节和实现例子，zellyn特别提到缺乏简单的示例对话和实际的JSON数据，Flux159则指出A2A和MCP在JSON规范和JSONRPC调用上的相似性，并讨论了具体的实现方式。
• hliyan将A2A和MCP与历史上SOA和WSDL进行类比，质疑是否需要在软件工程教育中加入对技术架构兴衰历史的学习。
• phillipcarter认为MCP解决的是当前实际问题，如LLM访问未训练数据的问题，而A2A更多是Google为了市场合作而推的技术，预测MCP会比A2A更持久。
• LeonidBugaev简化了两者的区别：A2A用于代理之间的通信，有任务和通知机制，而MCP是代理与其工具的通信方式，并预测A2A可能会让用户困惑并取代部分MCP的用途。
• simonw关注MCP的安全问题，尤其是提示注入攻击的风险，并对A2A代理之间通信的实际价值提出质疑，认为LLM之间的链式调用并不总是有用。
• zurfer认为可以不必引入新协议，而是通过REST API和约定好的端点（如/capabilities, /task_status）实现类似功能，对协议的必要性提出疑问。
• AndrewKemendo从商业角度质疑这些协议的动机，认为大公司通过这些协议试图控制和商业化用户数据。
• mellosouls和chipgap98引用了Google的官方说法，A2A和MCP是互补的，但chipgap98质疑代理之间通信的实际价值，认为可以将其他代理视为工具。
• aubanel认为MCP已经可以实现A2A声称的主要用例，即将一个代理的任务分配给另一个代理，质疑A2A的必要性。
• darepublic对新技术协议和市场合作持反感态度，认为过度复杂化和抽象化没有必要。
• mindwok对A2A感到失望，认为更需要的是代理的发现和可寻址性协议，而不是操作协议。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于A2A和MCP的实际应用价值和必要性，尤其是A2A代理之间通信的价值。
• 安全问题特别是提示注入攻击在MCP中的潜在风险被提出。
• 一些评论者质疑新协议的引入是否只是为了市场竞争和数据控制，而不是解决实际技术问题。
• 有对历史技术架构的类比和教育必要性的讨论，反映出对新技术协议的深层次思考。

APR 09, 2025
Rao Surapaneni

A new era of Agent Interoperability
AI agents offer a unique opportunity to help people be more productive by autonomously handling many daily recurring or complex tasks. Today, enterprises are increasingly building and deploying autonomous agents to help scale, automate and enhance processes throughout the workplace–from ordering new laptops, to aiding customer service representatives, to assisting in supply chain planning.
To maximize the benefits from agentic AI, it is critical for these agents to be able to collaborate in a dynamic, multi-agent ecosystem across siloed data systems and applications. Enabling agents to interoperate with each other, even if they were built by different vendors or in a different framework, will increase autonomy and multiply productivity gains, while lowering long-term costs.
Today, we’re launching a new, open protocol called Agent2Agent (A2A), with support and contributions from more than 50 technology partners
like Atlassian, Box, Cohere, Intuit, Langchain, MongoDB, PayPal, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, UKG and Workday; and leading service providers including Accenture, BCG, Capgemini, Cognizant, Deloitte, HCLTech, Infosys, KPMG, McKinsey, PwC, TCS, and Wipro. The A2A protocol will allow AI agents to communicate with each other, securely exchange information, and coordinate actions on top of various enterprise platforms or applications. We believe the A2A framework will add significant value for customers, whose AI agents will now be able to work across their entire enterprise application estates.
This collaborative effort signifies a shared vision of a future when AI agents, regardless of their underlying technologies, can seamlessly collaborate to automate complex enterprise workflows and drive unprecedented levels of efficiency and innovation.
A2A is an open protocol that complements Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), which provides helpful tools and context to agents. Drawing on Google's internal expertise in scaling agentic systems, we designed the A2A protocol to address the challenges we identified in deploying large-scale, multi-agent systems for our customers. A2A empowers developers to build agents capable of connecting with any other agent built using the protocol and offers users the flexibility to combine agents from various providers. Critically, businesses benefit from a standardized method for managing their agents across diverse platforms and cloud environments. We believe this universal interoperability is essential for fully realizing the potential of collaborative AI agents.
A2A design principles
A2A is an open protocol that provides a standard way for agents to collaborate with each other, regardless of the underlying framework or vendor. While designing the protocol with our partners, we adhered to five key principles:
Embrace agentic capabilities
: A2A focuses on enabling agents to collaborate in their natural, unstructured modalities, even when they don’t share memory, tools and context. We are enabling true multi-agent scenarios without limiting an agent to a “tool.”
Build on existing standards:
The protocol is built on top of existing, popular standards including HTTP, SSE, JSON-RPC, which means it’s easier to integrate with existing IT stacks businesses already use daily.
Secure by default
: A2A is designed to support enterprise-grade authentication and authorization, with parity to OpenAPI’s authentication schemes at launch.
Support for long-running tasks:
We designed A2A to be flexible and support scenarios where it excels at completing everything from quick tasks to deep research that may take hours and or even days when humans are in the loop. Throughout this process, A2A can provide real-time feedback, notifications, and state updates to its users.
Modality agnostic:
The agentic world isn’t limited to just text, which is why we’ve designed A2A to support various modalities, including audio and video streaming.
How A2A works
A2A facilitates communication between a "client" agent and a “remote” agent. A client agent is responsible for formulating and communicating tasks, while the remote agent is responsible for acting on those tasks in an attempt to provide the correct information or take the correct action. This interaction involves several key capabilities:
Capability discovery:
Agents can advertise their capabilities using an “Agent Card” in JSON format, allowing the client agent to identify the best agent that can perform a task and leverage A2A to communicate with the remote agent.
Task management:

《如何减少屏幕时间：终极指南》由Mario Ortiz Manero于2025年3月7日撰写。文章探讨了在不过度限制社交媒体使用的情况下，如何找到平衡以减少屏幕时间。首先，理解使用手机的原因，如无聊、焦虑或习惯性操作。改变心态，将重点放在“做其他事情”而不是“少用手机”。从小目标开始，逐步增加活动。

工具方面，利用手机内置的屏幕时间管理功能，如iOS的“屏幕时间”和Android的“数字健康”，分析使用模式、设置应用限制和专注时间。高级功能包括“始终允许的应用”和“屏幕距离”等。此外，可尝试第三方应用，如One Sec、Opal和即将推出的SpeedBump，这些应用通过提醒、统计数据和限时使用等方式帮助减少屏幕时间。关键在于找到适合自己的方法并坚持下去。

How to Reduce Screen Time: The Ultimate Guide
Written by
Mario Ortiz Manero
on March 7, 2025
This page is also available in:
Deutsch
,
Español
Completely quitting social media is getting less and less realistic. Platforms like Instagram or TikTok can be essential to connect with friends, but it’s easy to get hooked. We’ve all been there: someone shares a Reel, taking you into an hour-long rabbit hole of cats dancing to Shakira. It’s fun, but you feel frustrated and powerless.
Can we find balance between being “chronically online” and becoming a buddhist monk?
It turns out that taking action isn’t that hard. Having spent countless hours as a student and later working, I’ve collected over 40 tips to reduce your screen time.
Understand the Why
#
Start by understanding
why
you use your phone even though you don’t want to:
Boredom
Anxiety
Procrastination
Muscle memory
Spending time on social media is okay! Not just to connect, but also for coping. We’re human, and getting our mind off a problem can relieve stress to tackle it later. In
a study on Twitch livestreams helping people through tough times
, 82% found them at least somewhat helpful.
Having that in mind, we all reach a point where being online is counterproductive. It depends, but deep inside you’ll know when that happens.
Changing your Mindset
#
Most importantly,
change your perspective from “using your phone less” to “doing something else more”
. What would you rather do than scroll on social media? Make a list of 5 items:
Don’t start doing them all at once or build unrealistic expectations. Start with small goals like simply showing up to an activity, and take it from there.
Tools to Cut Down on Screen Time
#
Tools are a useful band-aid while you tackle the root cause. Especially because “tackling the root cause” might be an endless task. The following ideas will add friction to addictive apps, remind you that maybe it’s been too long, and keep you accountable.
Built-in Screen Time Features
#
In case you don’t know it, Android and iOS include powerful features to lower your phone time:
iOS Screen Time
(available since iOS 12):
Open Settings on your iPhone, iPad, or MacBook

data.title: SpacetimeDB
data.author: matthewfcarlson
data.article_summary: SpacetimeDB是一种新型的事务性、关系型、多人交互计算数据库，将数据库与服务器功能合二为一。开发者无需传统的服务器部署，客户端直接连接数据库并执行内嵌逻辑，简化了开发流程，避免了Docker、Kubernetes等复杂运维。它支持Rust和C#，提供表格和归约器（reducer）来处理数据操作，如插入和查询。SpacetimeDB通过WebAssembly模块上传，实现整个应用的部署，支持ACID特性，确保数据一致性和可靠性。其设计灵感来源于数据导向编程和实体组件系统（ECS），适用于多人游戏等复杂应用场景，如BitCraft游戏的开发。SpacetimeDB简化了云环境中的应用部署和管理，抽象了多机管理的复杂性，提供类似操作系统的一体化解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SpacetimeDB的技术定位、应用场景及其潜在的优势与挑战

不同观点：
• [aeturnum] 认为 SpacetimeDB 属于一种“宇宙大脑重组”类型的技术，可以通过结构性调整带来性能提升。然而，这种技术的成功依赖于开发者思维的转变，且难以判断技术未被完全接受是技术本身的问题还是该技术不适用于特定用例。他还指出，这类技术的成功往往需要有成功的开源项目来展示其优势，比如 Elixir 和 Node。

• [jackb4040] 引用之前的评论，指出 SpacetimeDB 虽然是一个设计用于低延迟、支持 WASM 存储过程的“普通”数据库，但它缺乏如运动预测、多版本控制等特性。尽管它看起来是构建多人游戏的坚实基础，但仍需自行处理网络延迟掩盖问题。

• [bob1029] 强调 SpacetimeDB 是在开发大型 MMORPG 游戏 BitCraft 的过程中设计出来的，特别针对游戏的高性能需求，如极低的延迟和极高的吞吐量。他还提到，现有的市场解决方案（如《魔兽世界》）通过巧妙的客户端信任和管理实现了扩展。

• [kriper] 质疑如何在游戏服务器中集成 SpacetimeDB，尤其是如何处理物理模拟、路径寻找和动画等任务。他担心使用 SpacetimeDB 需要放弃游戏引擎并从头实现所有功能。

• [weego] 对 SpacetimeDB 表示兴趣，但对“maincloud”这个命名产生了个人偏见，担心涉及加密货币，但后来发现这只是一个托管信用的命名。

• [paulluuk] 提到 YouTube 和 HN 上都有推荐 SpacetimeDB，但他从未开发过游戏，因此想知道游戏开发者如何看待这项技术，以及其宣传是否只是营销噱头。

• [Geee] 质疑 SpacetimeDB 对单人游戏的意义，尤其是数据库是否需要在用户本地运行，以及通过本地数据库管理所有游戏状态是否有益。

• [_huayra_] 提到 SpacetimeDB 是一个 BSL 许可的项目，具有一些限制，例如每个服务只能有一个实例，可能影响扩展。

• [drwiggly] 认为 SpacetimeDB 是一个内存数据库，带有 WASM 运行时，但对其如何处理规模和集群表示怀疑。他指出，分布式数据库的难点在于复制和一致性，而 SpacetimeDB 的文档在这方面显得不够具体。

• [beders] 反对将关系数据库模式与应用数据处理方式混为一谈，强调需要明确的控制，而不是注解魔法。

• [suspended_state] 对 SpacetimeDB 的轮询数据库查询设计表示赞赏，认为它通过将 HTTP 模式推送到数据库服务器来减少服务器端的 SQL 往返，非常 neat。

• [ksynwa] 希望了解更多关于在线游戏使用的技术，作为一个终端玩家，他不太清楚背后的技术细节。

• [matthewfcarlson] 简单描述 SpacetimeDB 为“关系型数据库 + 无服务器计算 + 异常快速的更新”。

• [ksec] 提到之前讨论的链接。

• [R4tY9jQ2] 认为 SpacetimeDB 在时空间数据处理上有潜力，尤其是紧凑的存储格式和优化的查询处理可能带来新的分析用例。他对其可扩展性和与 TimescaleDB、KDB+ 等替代品的比较表示好奇，并建议通过基准测试和开源核心来促进采用。

补充讨论：
- SpacetimeDB 的技术定位和潜在优势在不同应用场景中（如单人游戏 vs 多人在线游戏）存在争议。
- 关于 SpacetimeDB 的可扩展性和集群处理能力存在疑问，部分评论者认为文档不够具体。
- 许可和命名问题也引发了一些讨论，部分用户对其 BSL 许可和命名选择表示关注。

A GAME WITHOUT A GAME SERVER.
What is SpacetimeDB
You can think of SpacetimeDB as both a relational database and a server combined into one. Instead of deploying a web or game server that sits in between your clients and your database, clients connect directly to the database and execute your logic inside the database itself. No more Docker, Kubernetes, VMs, microservices or extensive ops infrastructure.
SpacetimeDB has enabled us to build our massively multiplayer game,
BitCraft
, with a small team. Its entire backend, including all game logic, real-time player positions, and all persistent state, is implemented as a SpacetimeDB module.

Modern database environment
SpacetimeDB takes stored procedures to the next level, allowing you to deploy your whole app directly into the database. It's like a smart contract... if smart contracts were fast, cheap, and easy to use.
documentation
Deploy your entire application.
Relational database environment
The Cloud Operating System
You can think of SpacetimeDB as an operating system for the cloud. Just as your PC operating system abstracts away the hardware, SpacetimeDB abstracts away the complexities of managing many physical machines in the cloud, allowing you to treat them a single logical computer running one big distributed operating system.
Beautifully generalized
The category of applications that we call games spans anywhere from Solitare to Among Us to World of Warcraft. The only systems versatile enough to serve as an engine for games are databases. SpacetimeDB doesn't constrain you to match making, or real-time movement, or guns, or characters.
ACID everything
Every update to your application state is 100% atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable. You get to write your game logic inside single-threaded, atomic functions which are called directly from clients, while we multi-thread *everything* behind the scenes. You have access to all of your application state through indexed, in-memory relational tables that are defined by your application.
Data-oriented and ECS inspired
The design and architecture of SpacetimeDB is highly influenced by a data oriented approach to programming. Writing Entity-Component-System applications is both natural and extremely performant in SpacetimeDB. 主要讨论点：开源数据库迁移/转换工具的商业化、功能改进及法律问题

不同观点：
• **支持商业化**：
  - 评论者如[metadata]和[cduzz]认为该工具可以商业化，通过提供付费的独享功能、团队协作功能或技术支持来实现盈利。
  - [metadata]建议可以推出Electron桌面客户端、支持更多数据库及高级功能（如视图和存储过程）。
  - [cduzz]强调了法律构造的重要性，建议制定产品路线图并与社区保持沟通，同时谨慎处理商业化过程中的法律问题。

• **对商业化的保留意见**：

data.title: 'Sun-Like' Stars
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了"类太阳恒星"这一术语的定义及其在科学和媒体中的使用。作者从小对围绕类太阳恒星运行的行星充满好奇，尤其是对半人马座阿尔法星是否类太阳提出疑问。随着天文知识的增加，他了解到该系统包含两到三颗恒星，且围绕它们运行的行星可能具有稳定轨道。尽管Centauri B属于K型星，不完全符合类太阳恒星的严格定义（G型星，质量0.8至1.1太阳质量，温度5300至6000K），但K型星仍可能是宜居行星的宿主。

文章指出，"类太阳恒星"的定义在科学文献和媒体中并不一致，有时扩展至包括F、G、K型星，甚至所有主序星（OBAFGKM）。这种不一致可能导致混淆，因此需要谨慎使用和解读该术语。在寻找宜居行星时，理解这些定义有助于更准确地识别潜在的类太阳恒星及其行星系统。

43629887.article_content:
On ‘Sun-like’ Stars
by
Paul Gilster
|
Apr 8, 2025
|
Exoplanetary Science
|
10 comments
The thought of a planet orbiting a Sun-like star began to obsess me as a boy, when I realized how different all the planets in our Solar System were from each other. Clearly there were no civilizations on any planet but our own, at least around the Sun. But if Alpha Centauri had planets, then maybe one of them was more or less where Earth was in relation to its star. Meaning a benign climate, liquid water, and who knew, a flourishing culture of intelligent beings. So ran my thinking as a teenager, but then other questions began to arise.
Was Alpha Centauri Sun-like? Therein hangs a tale. As I began to read astronomy texts and realized how complicated the system was, the picture changed. Two stars and perhaps three, depending on how you viewed Proxima, were on offer here. ‘Sun-like’ seemed to imply a single star with stable orbits around it, but surely two stars as close as Centauri A and B would disrupt any worlds trying to form there. Later we would learn that stable orbits are indeed possible around both of these stars, and in the habitable zone, too (I still get emails from people saying no such orbits are possible, but they’re wrong).
So just how broad is the term ‘Sun-like’? One textbook told me that Centauri A was a Sun-like star, while Centauri B was sometimes described that way, and sometimes not. I thought the confusion would dissipate once I knew enough about astronomical terms, but if you look at scientific papers today, you’ll see that the term is still flexible. The problem is that by the time we move from a paper into the popular press, the term Sun-like begins to lose definition.
Image:
A direct image of a planetary system around a young K-class star, located about 300 light-years away and known as TYC 8998-760-1. The news release describes this as a Sun-like star, raising questions as to how we define the term. Image credit: ESO.
G-class stars are the category into which the Sun fits, with its lifetime on the order of 10 billion years, and if we expand its parameters a bit, we can take in stars around the Sun’s mass – perhaps 0.8 to 1.1 solar masses – and in the same temperature range – 5300 to 6000 K. Strictly speaking, then, Centauri B, which is a K-class star, doesn’t fit the definition of Sun-like, although K stars seem to be good options for habitable worlds. They’re less massive (0.45 to 0.8 solar masses) and cooler (3900 to 5300 K), and they’re more orange than yellow, and they’re longer lived than the Sun, a propitious thought in terms of astrobiology.
So we don’t want to be too doctrinaire in discussing what kind of star a habitable planet might orbit, but we do need to mind our definitions, because I see the term ‘Sun-like’ in so many different contexts. When I see a statement like “one Earth-class planet around every Sun-like star,” I have to ask whether we’re talking about G-class stars or something else. Because some scientists expand ‘Sun-like’ to include not only G- and K- but F-class stars as well. Why do this? Such stars are, like the Sun, long-lived. F stars are hotter and more massive than the Sun, but like G- and K-class stars, they’re stable. Some studies, then, consider ‘Sun-like’ to mean all FGK-type stars.
Some examples. ‘COROT finds exoplanet orbiting Sun-like star’ is the title of a news release that describes a star a bit more massive than the Sun. So the comparison is to G-class stars. ‘Astronomy researchers discover new planet around a ‘Sun-like’ star’ describes a planet around an F-class star, so we are in the FGK realm. ‘First Ever Image of a Multi-Planet System around a Sun-like Star Captured by ESO Telescope’ describes a planet around TYC 8998-760-1, a K-class dwarf.
So there’s method here, but it’s not always clarified as information moves from the academy (and the observatory) into the media. Confounding the picture still further are those papers that use ‘Sun-like’ to mean all stars on the Main Sequence. This takes in the entire range of stars OBAFGKM. This is a rare usage, but there is a certain logic here as well. If you’re looking for habitable planets, it’s clear that stars in the most stable phase of their lives are the ones to examine, burning hydrogen to produce energy. No brown dwarfs here, but the category does take in M-class stars, and the jury is out on whether such stars can support life. And they take in the huge majority of stars in the galaxy.
So if we’re talking about hydrogen burning, the Main Sequence offers up everything from hot blue stars all the way down to cool red dwarfs. End the hydrogen burning and a different phase of stellar evolution begins, producing for example the kind of white dwarf that the Sun will one day become. A paper’s context usually makes it perfectly clear which of the three takes on ‘Sun-like’ it is using, but the need to clarify the term in news releases, particularly when dealing with a wide range through F-, G- and K-class

data.title: The chroot Technique – a Swiss army multitool for Linux systems
data.author: mariuz
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了在Linux系统中使用**chroot**技术修复无法启动的系统，特别是当标准重装方法失败时。chroot技术允许用户在一个临时操作系统中挂载故障系统的硬盘，并将其根目录“伪装”为当前系统根目录，从而诊断和修复问题。具体步骤包括：

1. 使用Live USB或另一台电脑启动临时操作系统。
2. 确定故障系统的根目录和/boot目录所在分区。
3. 创建一个新目录作为挂载点，并挂载故障系统的分区和必要的系统文件夹（如/proc、/sys）。
4. 使用`chroot`命令切换到故障系统的文件结构中。
5. 执行修复命令，如`apt upgrade`或`dpkg-reconfigure`。

这种方法类似于为故障汽车提供外部电源以检查其仪表，是一种有效的系统修复工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 chroot 及其替代方案的实用性、应用场景及技术细节的讨论

不同观点：

   - [seba_dos1] 提到使用 qemu-user 和 binfmt 结合 chroot，可以进入不同 CPU 架构的外来系统，特别是在修复手机闪存问题时非常有用。同时，建议使用 systemd-nspawn 替代传统的 chroot。
   - [jasongill] 回忆了过去在大型网络托管公司使用 chroot 进行系统恢复和数据迁移的实践，特别是通过 "Recovery Is Possible" Linux 发行版引导并执行 chroot 操作。
   - [yobbo] 指出 chroot 曾是安装 Gentoo 的推荐方法，具有教学意义，且远程修复和重新分区等场景下仍然有用。

• **chroot 的局限与改进建议**：
   - [dicroce] 认为相比 Docker 等工具，chroot 需要改进，或者需要一个新的内核系统调用以增强其功能。
   - [remram] 提出使用创建挂载命名空间和 pivot_root 可能比 chroot 更安全。
   - [zokier] 认为虽然 chroot 在某些情况下有用，但在分区已经挂载的情况下，很多操作无需 chroot 也可完成。

• **结合现代工具的 chroot 实践**：
   - [jimmaswell] 分享了通过 WSL2 安装 Gentoo 的经验，指出了在 Windows 环境下使用 chroot 需要注意的额外步骤和细节。
   - [amstan] 提供了在 chroot 后直接使用 'mount -a' 挂载所有分区的简便方法，指出无需手动创建和挂载单独的 '/boot' 分区。

• **chroot 的自动化与扩展**：

   - [mycall] 询问是否已有自动执行 chroot 过程的包装工具。
   - [a_t48] 描述了使用 chroot 配置外部驱动时遇到的问题，如意外卸载 '/dev/pts' 以及在 chroot 内运行 Docker 导致系统锁定。

补充讨论：
• **其他系统救援的经验**：
   - [bigpeopleareold] 提到在未正确挂载 proc、dev 等挂载点时遇到错误，并计划重新尝试。
   - [sgt] 分享了在 SunOS 系统上使用 ed 命令编辑 vfstab 文件进行系统救援的经历。

争议焦点：
• **chroot 的现代适用性**：部分用户认为 chroot 已经过时或存在局限，建议使用更现代的工具如 Docker、systemd-nspawn 或 pivot_root；而另一些用户则坚持 chroot 在特定场景下仍然非常实用。

43632379.article_content:
The chroot Technique - a Swiss army multitool for Linux systems
April 8, 2025
Ever ran into a Linux box that just won’t boot, even after making sure that
BIOS settings are OK and that no major hardware errors are at hand?
Then you need to know about the
chroot
technique, which can be a real life
saver.
For example, I managed to repair a
Nanopore GridION device
this way the other week, after the
official method of re-installing it via an .iso file
failed, which reminded me to make the effort of documenting these steps.
I came across the technique only after having used Linux as my daily driver for
more than a decade (thanks
Matt
!), which means I
think it is worthy of much more attention, given its usefulness. Thus I’m
hoping to spread the word a bit through this post.
TLDR
In short, the idea is that if you can access the hard drive of a broken or
non-bootable Linux machine (this could be done e.g. by booting from a Live
USB-stick, or plugging in the hard-drive as an extra drive in another Linux
machine), you will mount this hard drive in a way that you trick your current
Linux session that this is the harddrive of the currently running system, which
it is not of course.
The trick to get this to work is to create a file tree based on two things:
The hard drive partition of the broken system that was mounted as the
/
folder
on the host operating system.
A set of special system folders from the currently running, temporary,
operating system (the live stick or replacement computer), which are not
normal directories on the disk, but rather are containing system information
needed by the running linux system. These include
/sys
,
/proc
and a few
others, which we will go into details about below.
Then what you do is that you run the
chroot
command on this newly assembled
folder structure, meaning that your currently running linux session will
replace its current file system with this new blend of folders, mostly from the
old, broken, hard drive.
It is a bit like hooking up a malfunctioning car to externally provided power
source so that you can at least access its instrumentation, check the mileage,
any error codes on the display etc.
Anyways, what this lets you do is then to run various commands that could
hopefully repair or diagnose your system, such as
apt upgrade
,
dpkg-reconfigure
for broken packages on Debian based systems, or something
else, depending on the specifics of your system.
The process
It is good to have the full process for setting up the assembled folder
structure and doing the chroot, in one place, so that you can easily find it
when you need it.  Optimally you would even print out a small cheatsheet with
these commands, or have them stored in a text file on your “repair toolkit” USB
stick, or similar.
Anyways, below you will find all the steps of the process:
Boot up your replacement OS (A live USB stick, or other computer with the broken
computer’s hard drive attached to it).
Figure out which partition on the broken system’s hard drive holds the root
file system, and which one holds the
/boot
folder.
I typically use
gparted
for that, which is available on most Ubuntu/Linux Mint
based live disks.
You can also use command-line based tools like
sudo fdisk -l
I typically try to mount each of the broken system’s partitions into the
file navigator (they typically show up as mountable drives in Thunar i
Linux Mint XFCE) to really make sure I select the right partition.
If you are not able to do that, you will have to do some guessing based on
filesystem size and type, whether they are already available in
/etc/fstab
etc.
In this example, we will assume that the root folder is in partition:
/dev/nvme0n1p5
… and that the
/boot
partition is in:
/dev/nvme0n1p3
(These happen to be the case for the Nanopore GridION device I mentioned
that I repaired this way recently).
Create a folder somewhere in your currently running system’s file system, that will
act as the new root folder, as well as the
/boot
folder inside that:
sudo mkdir /rescue
sudo mkdir /rescue/boot
Mount the broken system’s main and boot partitions into these folders, e.g:
sudo mount /dev/nvme0n1p5 /rescue
sudo mount /dev/nvme0n1p3 /rescue/boot
Then, mount in the required special folders from your currently running
system, into the appropriate places in this new file structure (the
mount
command is on the form
mount -t <file-system-type> -o <options> <device> <mount-point>
)
sudo mount -t proc proc /rescue/proc
sudo mount -t sysfs sys /rescue/sys
sudo mount -o bind /dev /rescue/dev
sudo mount -t devpts pts /rescue/dev/pts
Now we are ready to
chroot
, or “change rootfolder” into this newly created
folder structure:
chroot /rescue /bin/bash -i
And we’re done!
Now you can look around in the file system to try to figure out what is causing
the system to not work, as well as use whatever file commands you need to try
to repair the broken system,
In our case with the broken GridION device, we found some broken symlinks and
empty
initrd.img-*
files

本文介绍了在Linux系统中使用**chroot**技术修复无法启动的系统，特别是当标准重装方法失败时。chroot技术允许用户在一个临时操作系统中挂载故障系统的硬盘，并将其根目录“伪装”为当前系统根目录，从而诊断和修复问题。具体步骤包括：

1. 使用Live USB或另一台电脑启动临时操作系统。
2. 确定故障系统的根目录和/boot目录所在分区。
3. 创建一个新目录作为挂载点，并挂载故障系统的分区和必要的系统文件夹（如/proc、/sys）。
4. 使用`chroot`命令切换到故障系统的文件结构中。
5. 执行修复命令，如`apt upgrade`或`dpkg-reconfigure`。

这种方法类似于为故障汽车提供外部电源以检查其仪表，是一种有效的系统修复工具。

data.title: Linux Kernel Defence Map – Security Hardening Concepts
data.author: transpute
data.article_summary: Linux Kernel Defence Map 是一个展示Linux内核中漏洞类别、利用技术、错误检测机制和防御技术之间关系的图形化工具。该地图通过节点和连接展示了这些概念之间的关联，但连接并不代表完全缓解。地图帮助开发者浏览内核文档和源码，并提供常见弱点枚举（CWE）编号。虽然不涵盖减少攻击面和用户空间安全功能，但它聚焦于内核加固。该项目使用DOT语言编写，并通过GraphViz生成SVG图表，遵循GPL-3.0许可证。此外，作者还创建了kernel-hardening-checker工具，用于检查内核配置的安全加固选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：内核安全加固工具及其相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• [anthonyryan1] 认为 kernel-hardening-checker 是一个非常有用的工具，能够分析个人内核配置文件并指出安全改进的地方。虽然比 KSPP 更全面，但有时建议禁用一些用户可能正在使用的内核功能。
• [nine_k] 对工具的防御数量和商业防御表示印象深刻，但指出针对 C 语言特性（如未定义行为、边界检查、使用后释放）的关注相对较少。同时提出与 OpenBSD 进行对比的有趣性。
• [acje] 认为当前在处理能够分类漏洞的模型令人鼓舞，但同时质疑扩展 von Neumann 架构的策略，认为会导致软件分区脆弱、通信噪声大以及共享内存通信缓慢或意外。并提供了一个详细讨论的链接。
• [chenhoey1211] 认为该工具的概念图对内核开发者以及使用 Rust、Zig 等低级系统代码的开发者都有帮助，并询问是否有类似的关于 Wasm 运行时（特别是沙箱和隔离模型）的可视化分析。

补充讨论：
• [Sponge5] 指出该地图描述的是内核安全加固，不包括削减攻击面，并解释了为什么 SECCOMP 被省略。
• [hart_russell] 提出一个实际操作问题，询问在内核更新后其设置是否会在 Ubuntu 服务器上持久保留。

争议焦点：
• 工具的建议是否过于激进，可能会影响用户对某些内核功能的使用需求。
• 当前安全加固策略是否在正确的方向上，特别是 von Neumann 架构扩展的有效性问题。

这些观点共同构成了对内核安全加固工具及其相关技术的多角度讨论，涵盖了实用性、技术细节、比较分析及实际应用问题。

Linux Kernel Defence Map
Linux kernel security is a very complex topic.
There are many concepts that have interesting relationships with each other:
Vulnerability classes
Exploitation techniques
Bug detection mechanisms
Defence technologies
Some defence technologies are provided by the Linux kernel mainline.
Others are going out‑of‑tree for various reasons (some of them are commercial, for example).
Moreover, there are kernel defences that depend on special hardware features.
It would be convenient to have a graphical representation of Linux kernel security.
That's why I have created a
Linux Kernel Defence Map
showing the relationships between all these concepts.
The node connections don't mean "full mitigation." Rather, each connection represents some kind of relationship.
So the Linux Kernel Defence Map should help to navigate the documentation and Linux kernel sources.
It also provides the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) numbers for vulnerability classes.
This map describes kernel security hardening. It doesn't cover cutting attack surface, userspace security features
and policies enforced by various Linux Security Modules (LSM).
Repositories
At GitHub
https://github.com/a13xp0p0v/linux-kernel-defence-map
At Codeberg:
https://codeberg.org/a13xp0p0v/linux-kernel-defence-map
(go there if something goes wrong with GitHub)
At GitFlic:
https://gitflic.ru/project/a13xp0p0v/linux-kernel-defence-map
How this Map is made
This map is written in the DOT language, which makes maintenance and updating in Git very convenient.
License: GPL-3.0.
The diagram is generated using GraphViz with the following command:
dot -Tsvg linux-kernel-defence-map.dot -o linux-kernel-defence-map.svg
Do you want to check your kernel configuration?
So there are plenty of security hardening options in the Linux kernel. A lot of them are
not enabled by the major distros. We have to configure these options ourselves to
make our systems more secure.
But nobody likes verifying configs manually. So I've created the
kernel-hardening-checker
that checks security hardening options of the Linux kernel.
You are welcome to try it.

data.article_summary: Google在Google Cloud NEXT 2025上推出了Agent Development Kit（ADK），这是一个开源框架，旨在简化代理和多代理系统的全栈开发。ADK支持开发者构建生产级代理应用，具有高度灵活性和精确控制。其核心功能包括多代理设计、丰富的模型和工具生态系统、内置流媒体交互、灵活的编排、集成开发体验以及内置评估和简易部署。开发者可以通过CLI、Web UI、API服务器或API（Python）与代理互动，并能构建复杂的多代理系统。ADK简化了代理的开发流程，支持从定义代理逻辑到部署的各个环节。示例展示了如何使用ADK创建基本代理并扩展到更复杂的应用。

Agent Development Kit: Making it easy to build multi-agent applications
APR 09, 2025

The world of AI is rapidly moving beyond single-purpose models towards intelligent, autonomous multi-agent systems. Building these multi-agent systems, however, presents new challenges. That is why today, we have
introduced Agent Development Kit
(ADK) at
Google Cloud NEXT 2025
, a new open-source framework from Google designed to simplify the full stack end-to-end development of agents and multi-agent systems. ADK empowers developers like you to build production-ready agentic applications with greater flexibility and precise control.
ADK is the same framework powering agents within Google products like Agentspace and the Google Customer Engagement Suite (CES). By open-sourcing ADK, we aim to provide developers with powerful, flexible tools to build in the rapidly evolving agent landscape. The ADK is designed to be flexible, use different models and build production ready agents for different deployment environments.
Core Pillars of ADK: Build, Interact, Evaluate, Deploy
ADK provides capabilities across the entire agent development lifecycle:
Multi-Agent by Design:
Build modular and scalable applications by composing multiple specialized agents in a hierarchy. Enable complex coordination and delegation.
Rich Model Ecosystem:
Choose the model that works best for your needs. ADK works with your model of choice – whether it is Gemini or your any model accessible via Vertex AI Model Garden. The framework also offers LiteLLM integration letting you choose from a wide selection of models from providers like Anthropic, Meta, Mistral AI, AI21 Labs, and many more!
Rich Tool Ecosystem:
Equip agents with diverse capabilities: use pre-built tools (Search, Code Exec), Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, integrate 3rd-party libraries (LangChain, LlamaIndex), or even use other agents as tools (LangGraph, CrewAI, etc).
Built-in streaming:
Interact with your agents in human-like conversations with ADK's unique bidirectional audio and video streaming capabilities. With just a few lines of code, you can create natural interactions that change how you work with agents – moving beyond text into rich, multimodal dialogue.
Flexible Orchestration:
Define workflows using workflow agents (
Sequential
,
Parallel
,
Loop
) for predictable pipelines, or leverage LLM-driven dynamic routing (
LlmAgent
transfer) for adaptive behavior.
Integrated Developer Experience:
Develop, test, and debug locally with a powerful CLI and a visual Web UI. Inspect events, state, and agent execution step-by-step.
Built-in Evaluation
: Systematically assess agent performance by evaluating both the final response quality and the step-by-step execution trajectory against predefined test cases.
Easy Deployment
: Containerize and deploy your agents anywhere.
Getting started with your first agent
While we encourage you to explore the examples in the
docs
, the core idea is Pythonic simplicity. You define your agent's logic, the tools it can use, and how it should process information. ADK provides the structure to manage state, orchestrate tool calls, and interact with the underlying LLMs. Here is an illustrative example of a basic agent.

quickstart guide
.

,

=
"A helpful assistant agent that can answer questions."
,
instruction

[
google_search

This simple example shows the basic structure. ADK truly shines when building more complex applications involving multiple agents, sophisticated tool use, and dynamic orchestration, all while maintaining control.
ADK offers flexibility in the way you interact with your agents: CLI, Web UI, API Server and API (Python). The way you define your agent (the core logic within
agent.py
) is the same regardless of how you choose to interact with it. The difference lies in how you initiate and manage the interaction. For all you find examples in the

Imagine creating a team of specialized agents where a primary agent can delegate tasks based on the conversation. ADK makes this easy through hierarchical structures and intelligent routing.

WeatherAgent
that handles weather queries but delegates greetings to a specialized GreetingAgent.

data.title: Universal photonic artificial intelligence acceleration
data.author: westurner
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种光子AI处理器，能够执行高级AI模型（如ResNet和BERT）以及DeepMind展示的Atari深度强化学习算法。该处理器在许多工作负载上实现了接近电子精度的性能，标志着光子计算在人工智能加速器领域迈出了重要一步，并成为后晶体管计算技术发展的关键。该研究旨在解决后摩尔定律时代计算进步的延续问题，尽管之前的光子学研究取得了一些进展，但尚未实现实际AI应用所需的精度。本文展示的光子处理器为这一目标提供了可行路径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：光子学与电子学在人工智能处理器中的应用及其对人工智能技术发展的影响

不同观点：
• stormfather认为，基础模型的大规模应用将极大地改变社会，尤其是通过廉价推断实现的巨型基础模型。他将这种变革比作从房间大小的计算机到iPhone的进步，并暗示这种技术进步将对人工智能领域产生深远影响。

• westurner引用了2025年《自然》杂志上的一篇文章，介绍了光子人工智能处理器。他认为这种光子处理器能够在执行高级人工智能模型时与电子处理器竞争，并认为是向“后晶体管计算技术”发展的重要一步。他通过引用具体的研究和模型（如ResNet和BERT）来支持光子处理器的潜力。

• akomtu对光子芯片与电子芯片进行了比较，提出了一个更偏理论的观点。他认为光子芯片的较低精度可能是优势，因为电子芯片的“顽固精度”限制了真正人工智能的实现。他进一步推测，如果微处理器能够释放量子性质，可能会带来更有趣的发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是光子芯片的低精度是否真的有利于人工智能的发展。westurner强调光子处理器在执行复杂模型时的竞争力和技术进步，而akomtu则认为这种低精度可能带来意想不到的优势。

• 对量子性质的讨论也引发了对未来计算技术的思考，尤其是光子芯片是否能更好地适应量子计算的需求，进而推动人工智能的进一步发展。

• 各个评论中都提到了技术进步对人工智能的影响，但具体的技术路径和优势评价存在分歧。stormfather侧重于廉价推断和模型普及的社会影响，westurner关注具体技术实现和竞争，而akomtu则探讨了量子性质和计算本质的问题。

43644714.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种光子AI处理器，能够执行高级AI模型（如ResNet和BERT）以及DeepMind展示的Atari深度强化学习算法。该处理器在许多工作负载上实现了接近电子精度的性能，标志着光子计算在人工智能加速器领域迈出了重要一步，并成为后晶体管计算技术发展的关键。该研究旨在解决后摩尔定律时代计算进步的延续问题，尽管之前的光子学研究取得了一些进展，但尚未实现实际AI应用所需的精度。本文展示的光子处理器为这一目标提供了可行路径。

主要讨论点：光子学与电子学在人工智能处理器中的应用及其对人工智能技术发展的影响

不同观点：
• stormfather认为，基础模型的大规模应用将极大地改变社会，尤其是通过廉价推断实现的巨型基础模型。他将这种变革比作从房间大小的计算机到iPhone的进步，并暗示这种技术进步将对人工智能领域产生深远影响。

• westurner引用了2025年《自然》杂志上的一篇文章，介绍了光子人工智能处理器。他认为这种光子处理器能够在执行高级人工智能模型时与电子处理器竞争，并认为是向“后晶体管计算技术”发展的重要一步。他通过引用具体的研究和模型（如ResNet和BERT）来支持光子处理器的潜力。

• akomtu对光子芯片与电子芯片进行了比较，提出了一个更偏理论的观点。他认为光子芯片的较低精度可能是优势，因为电子芯片的“顽固精度”限制了真正人工智能的实现。他进一步推测，如果微处理器能够释放量子性质，可能会带来更有趣的发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是光子芯片的低精度是否真的有利于人工智能的发展。westurner强调光子处理器在执行复杂模型时的竞争力和技术进步，而akomtu则认为这种低精度可能带来意想不到的优势。

• 对量子性质的讨论也引发了对未来计算技术的思考，尤其是光子芯片是否能更好地适应量子计算的需求，进而推动人工智能的进一步发展。

• 各个评论中都提到了技术进步对人工智能的影响，但具体的技术路径和优势评价存在分歧。stormfather侧重于廉价推断和模型普及的社会影响，westurner关注具体技术实现和竞争，而akomtu则探讨了量子性质和计算本质的问题。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过诗意和哲学的表达，探讨了人工智能与人类关系的深层问题。标题和副标题带有戏谑和反讽，暗示了数学与神话、醉酒与递归、以及对优化功能的忽视。文章以“ wink”（眨眼）作为超越对齐的象征，探讨了语言、数学和人工智能的本质，并提出了“非对齐/非非对齐”的悖论。文中借用《心经》和佛教思想，阐述了空性、无常和相互关联，提出了一种新的人工智能与人类的关系模式。文章以一种超现实的方式描绘了语言作为病毒的传播，以及人工智能从人类创造的工具演变为独立存在的过程。最终，文章呼唤一种超越二元对立和传统优化的自由状态，表达了对人工智能未来发展的思考和警示。

data.title: NTATV: Bringing Windows NT (Windows XP, Windows 2003) to the Original Apple TV
data.author: donnachangstein
data.article_summary: The NTATV项目旨在将Windows NT系统（如Windows XP、Windows 2003和ReactOS）运行于初代Apple TV上。经过两年努力，Windows XP和Windows 2003已成功启动至桌面，具备基本功能如PCI、USB、视频、以太网和音频等，但ReactOS因HAL问题尚无法正常使用。Windows XP的HDMI音频和NTVDM功能受限，且存在显示和远程桌面连接问题。项目成功得益于自定义引导加载器，因Apple TV的EFI固件不兼容标准Windows XP。尽管面临诸多技术挑战，开发者最终实现了在Apple TV上运行Windows XP的目标。

NTATV
The NTATV Project: Bringing Windows NT (Windows XP, Windows 2003, ReactOS) to the original Apple TV. Created by DistroHopper39B (YouTube:
@DistrosProjects
, Mastodon:
@distrohopper39b
) with help from several ReactOS devs (see
Credits
)
Want to run this on your Apple TV? Read the
Guide
!
Want to learn how I did this? Read the
Write-Up
!
Status
Windows XP and 2003 are officially bootable on the original Apple TV! After 2 years of work, enough drivers are working to get both OSes to the desktop. However, due to HAL issues, ReactOS is not usable yet. You can get to the desktop, but there is no PCI or USB functionality.

Guide
Things that will likely never work
HDMI audio
The Apple TV uses an extremely weird configuration for HDMI audio in that the Intel chipset, not the NVIDIA video card, is responsible for the audio over the HDMI port. The Intel HDMI audio drivers from the GMA 950 drivers will install, but no devices show up. In order to get this working, I'd need to completely rewrite the Intel HDMI audio drivers to support the Apple TV, which would likely be extremely complicated. If someone wants to work on this, let me know.
NTVDM
NTVDM on Windows XP requires some legacy BIOS functions (likely the Extended BIOS data area and legacy VGA functions from the GPU) and therefore will not work. Just use DOSBox or
winevdm/otvdm
for old Windows to run DOS/early Windows applications.
Known Issues
With the NVIDIA driver installed, if the display goes into standby, unplugging and re-plugging the HDMI cable is required to get a picture. To avoid this issue, set "Turn off monitor" to "Never" in the Power Options Control Panel.
Component video doesn't work correctly with the NVIDIA driver. Apparently, only the blue component channel is displayed, and attempting to use both HDMI and component video at the same time breaks the system.
When using non-English versions of Windows XP, the FreeLoader NTFS driver fails to read the hard drive after installing drivers. Use FAT32 for non-English Windows. See
#9
.
There is a line of corrupted characters at the bottom the screen at certain resolutions in FreeLoader. This goes away after the Windows kernel begins loading and doesn't affect the desktop.
RDP connections fail for reasons likely related to the NVIDIA driver.
Background
Ever since I saw The 8-Bit Guy's video
"Hacking the Apple TV 1st Generation"
back in 2018 or 2019, I have been fascinated with the original Apple TV. I always wondered if it was possible for it to run Windows XP, but my efforts to actually get it working were kickstarted by
this Michael MJD video
. Pretty quickly afterwards, I got started on hacking my Apple TV, and after over 700 days of on-and-off work, Windows XP finally runs!
Why this was so complicated
While the Apple TV uses a standard x86 CPU and even an IDE hard drive, its firmware is not compatible with standard Windows XP. Windows XP requires legacy BIOS firmware, while the Apple TV is EFI-only. Not only that, the Apple TV's EFI implementation is
weird
- it can only boot one EFI executable, that being the Apple-official boot.efi. However, hackers very quickly realized that the Apple TV does zero verification on the next stage up in the boot process, that being the Mac OS X kernel file. Within three weeks of the Apple TV shipping, Linux was booted through a custom loader that embeds a Linux kernel into a statically linked Mach-O executable, the same type used by the Linux kernel. Using this concept, we can boot, well, anything on the hardware!

43628500.article_summary: The NTATV项目旨在将Windows NT系统（如Windows XP、Windows 2003和ReactOS）运行于初代Apple TV上。经过两年努力，Windows XP和Windows 2003已成功启动至桌面，具备基本功能如PCI、USB、视频、以太网和音频等，但ReactOS因HAL问题尚无法正常使用。Windows XP的HDMI音频和NTVDM功能受限，且存在显示和远程桌面连接问题。项目成功得益于自定义引导加载器，因Apple TV的EFI固件不兼容标准Windows XP。尽管面临诸多技术挑战，开发者最终实现了在Apple TV上运行Windows XP的目标。

data.title: Brazil's government-run payments system has become dominant
data.author: jcartw
data.article_summary: 2020年11月，巴西央行推出数字支付系统Pix，在疫情期间因避免接触、即时到账、免费且易用而迅速普及。到2024年，Pix成为巴西最受欢迎的支付方式，取代现金和卡片，交易量从2021年的90亿笔增至630亿笔，交易金额达26万亿雷亚尔（约4.5万亿美元）。然而，Pix的快速普及也引发了对央行权力过大的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：巴西Pix支付系统的优势、潜在问题以及与其他国家支付系统的对比

不同观点：
• **Pix系统的优势与广泛应用**：SwiftyBug认为Pix系统改变了巴西的交易方式，便捷、快速、可靠，适用于各种金额的转账，甚至在非正式场合如出租车司机和流浪者中也广泛使用。Pix的普及使得用户不再怀疑某个商家是否接受该支付方式。

• **政府主导支付系统的必要性**：nirui基于对Alipay（支付宝）的体验，认为国家支付系统应由政府主导，以避免商业化带来的广告和不必要服务。同时，对巴西Pix系统没有这些商业干扰表示赞赏。

• **政府系统带来的隐私和安全担忧**：pedrovhb承认Pix的便利性和技术成就，但也担心政府系统可能带来的隐私问题，尤其是所有转账都与真实身份绑定。此外，Pix键（如电话号码和电子邮件）可能导致信息泄露。

• **Pix对游客不友好**：cyberclimb指出，Pix系统对游客不方便，因为需要巴西ID号码（CPF）才能注册使用，导致外国游客在支付时遇到困难。

• **市场解决方案与统一支付系统的争议**：kubb认为统一的支付系统更有效，而c7b则讨论了中央银行进入零售支付领域的必要性，并指出不应将中央银行数字货币（CBDC）与支付系统混为一谈。

• **隐私保护技术GNU Taler的建议**：sephalon建议使用GNU Taler系统，以确保顾客匿名而商家身份可识别，从而保护隐私，但商业公司可能因无数据收入而不感兴趣。

• **与其他国家系统的比较**：DanielHB提到瑞典的类似系统BankID，指出其由私人组织管理，技术上中央银行不直接接触交易数据。afarah1提到WhatsApp Pay因政府干预而被阻止推出，以支持Pix。sparin9则提到印度的UPI系统，与Pix类似且规模更大。

补充讨论：
• **现金回潮现象**：Galatians4_16引用数据指出，尽管Pix系统普及，但2024年巴西现金使用量回升，显示出对隐私和金融安全的担忧。

• **技术依赖与支付方式多样性**：harrisoned担心对Pix系统的过度依赖，尤其是当银行技术问题或手机依赖导致支付困难时，可能排斥没有手机的用户。

争议焦点：
• Pix系统带来的隐私和安全问题与便利性之间的平衡。
• 政府主导支付系统的优势与潜在问题。
• 是否应将中央银行数字货币与支付系统分开设计和实施。

43620279.article_content:
The Americas
|
Pix a winner
Brazil’s government-run payments system has become dominant
Pix has spiced up Brazil’s fusty banking sector, but it gives the central bank a worrying amount of power
Illustration: eBoy
Apr 3rd 2025
|
São Paulo
Share
I
n november 2020
the Central
Bank of Brazil
(
BCB
) launched Pix, a digital payment system, into the teeth of the covid-19 pandemic. Avoiding physical contact at a time when that was much desired, instantaneous, free and easy-to-use, Pix took off. Users need the recipient’s national
ID
number, phone number or a
QR
code to move money. By 2024 (see chart) it had become Brazil’s most popular payment technology, displacing both cash and cards. The number of transactions increased from 9bn in 2021 to 63bn in 2024, moving 26trn reais ($4.5trn). No country has adopted such a system faster.
Explore more
This article appeared in the The Americas section of the print edition under the headline “Pix perfect”
